items.name: Acoustic Guitar
items.description: A playable acoustic guitar used to attract ARC's attention, and impress other Raiders.
items.article:
The Acoustic Guitar is an instrument used to play melodies, which can attract nearby ARCs. Other Raiders can also play along with instruments such as the Recorder or Shaker. While playing, actions that require both hands are not possible.

  • It can be purchased from Shani for 70 coins, with a limit of one per day.
  • One is obtained upon completing the project Trophy Display.
  • It is also found on page 3 of Decks: Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie.

items.name: Action Economy
items.description: The Hairpin wastes very little motion between shots. That sort of efficiency gets more interesting once a scope is involved.

items.name: Adrenaline Shot
items.description: A serum that fully restores stamina and temporarily increases stamina regeneration.
items.article:
The Adrenaline Shot is a quick-use item that completely restores your stamina and temporarily makes it regenerate faster. This helps you keep moving or use stamina-draining abilities more often when you need to.

These shots can be found by scavenging in the environment, crafted at a Medical Lab or with the In-Round Crafting skill, or purchased from Lance for 900 coins.

items.name: Advanced ARC Powercell
items.description: Very valuable resource that drops from certain ARC enemies.
items.article:
The Advanced ARC Powercell is a resource item scavenged from ARCs like the Bastion, Courier, and Sentinel.

It is used in crafting various supplies at Workbench and Medical Lab. This item can also be recycled to gain other resources.

items.name: Advanced Camera
items.description: A more advanced camera with a few extra bells and whistles.

items.name: Advanced Camera Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft an Advanced Camera

items.name: Advanced Electrical Components
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.flavor_text: Used to craft: Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive), Combat Mk. 3 (Flanking), Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive), Looting Mk. 3 (Cautious), Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing)
items.article:
Advanced Electrical Components are a refined material primarily used to craft various items and to upgrade your Hideout.

You can acquire these components by scavenging them from the environment or by looting arcs. They can also be crafted at the Refiner.

items.name: Advanced Mechanical Components
items.description: Used to craft advanced weapons. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article:
Advanced Mechanical Components are a refined material primarily used for crafting and upgrading items. They support your weapon crafting at the Gunsmith in your Hideout, enabling the creation of various advanced weapons and high-end components.

  • You can find this item by defeating specific ARCs such as the Queen.
  • It can also be looted from various containers or environmental spots during your raids.
  • Another way is to craft it yourself at a Refiner using other materials.

This item can be recycled for resources.

items.name: Agave
items.description: A piece of an agave leaf. Can be used to regain a small amount of health.
items.article: Agave is an uncommon healing item that helps Raiders regain a small amount of health over time when consumed. It can be found by harvesting agave plants in the Dam Battlegrounds map and the outskirts of the Buried City map. Raiders can also scavenge for it inside wicker baskets. This item can also be used to craft healing supplies.

items.name: Agave Juice
items.description: A concoction that temporarily increases stamina regeneration, at a small initial cost to health.
items.article: Agave Juice is a consumable item that Raiders can use to temporarily increase their stamina regeneration, while taking a small amount of health damage at the start. This helps Raiders quickly regain stamina during raids and it can only be crafted in-raid.

items.name: Air Freshener
items.description: May be worth a few coins.
items.article: The Air Freshener is a trinket that Raiders collect. Its primary role is to be sold for coins, offering a simple way to earn funds during your raids. This item also has a secondary use as a crafting component: it can be combined with other materials to create crafted items, a process that takes place directly during an active raid. You can obtain it by thoroughly searching the environment and looting various containers.

items.name: Alarm Clock
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Alarm Clock is a resource Raiders can find by searching and looting within residential areas throughout the various maps. Its main use is to be recycled for basic crafting materials, which are helpful for crafting new gear or upgrading existing items at a crafting workbench in your Hideout.

items.name: Alien Duck
items.description: A long, long way from home.
items.flavor_text: Can be thrown to create noise.
items.article: The Alien Duck is a decorative item, a variant of the Rubber Duck. It serves to personalize your Raider Den in your Hideout, or you can throw it to create noise, which can be used as a distraction. You can obtain this item by scavenging inside chimneys when the "Bird City" event is active. Other similar collectible duck variants include the Doodly Duck, Familiar Duck, Flashy Duck, Gentle Duck, and Tropical Duck.

items.name: Ancient Fort Security Code
items.description: Temporary security code to unlock the main gate.
items.flavor_text: Can only be used during Locked Gate
items.article: The Ancient Fort Security Code is a temporary code used to unlock a main gate within the Ancient Fort area during the 'Locked Gate' map condition. You need four of these codes to open the gate. Find this item in lootable containers located in the Ancient Fort area of the Blue Gate map. To use a code, go to the Gate Control Room on the Blue Gate map, enter the building, and submit it at one of the four terminals. Submitting a code consumes it and activates the terminal which helps to open the Locked Gate.

items.name: Angled Grip I
items.description: Slightly reduces horizontal recoil.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Arpeggio, II toro, Venator, Bobcat, Tempest, Vulcano

items.flavor_text: 20% Reduced Horizontal Recoil
items.article: The Angled Grip I is a weapon modification designed to improve how steadily you can hold your weapon while aiming. It helps reduce horizontal recoil, making it easier to control your shots. Weapon modifications, including grips, can be found by searching through various containers during raids, or they can be crafted at the appropriate station.

items.name: Angled Grip II
items.description: Moderately reduces horizontal recoil.
items.flavor_text: 30% Reduced Horizontal Recoil
items.article: The Angled Grip II is a weapon attachment that helps reduce the sideways kick of your weapon when you shoot. You can obtain this grip by crafting it at the Gunsmith once you have the Angled Grip II Blueprint. The blueprint can be found by searching various containers or purchased from the vendor Shani for 100 coins, with a limit of two per day.

items.name: Angled Grip II Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft an Angled Grip II
items.article: The Angled Grip II Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Angled Grip II weapon modification at a Gunsmith workbench, which helps reduce a weapon's horizontal recoil. Once you learn it by using it in Speranza, you can craft the modification. Raiders can obtain this blueprint by scavenging residential containers found across all maps. It is also available as a reward from Weekly Trials or can be purchased from the vendor Shani for coins.

items.name: Angled Grip III
items.description: Significantly reduces horizontal recoil.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Arpeggio, II toro, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest, Vulcano, Aphelion

items.flavor_text: 40% Reduced Horizontal Recoil - 30% Reduced ADS Speed
items.article: The Angled Grip III is a weapon modification designed to improve your shooting accuracy by significantly reducing your weapon's sideways movement during firing. You can craft it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1 using the Angled Grip III blueprint. Keeping track of blueprints is easier with the Needed Items Tracker. Another way to obtain it is by purchasing it directly from the vendor Tian Wen for 15,000 coins, although he only has one available for sale each day. Once you have it, it can be recycled for general resources.

items.name: Angled Grip III Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft an Angled Grip III
items.article: The Angled Grip III Blueprint is a blueprint that unlocks the crafting recipe for the Angled Grip III at a Workbench. You can find this blueprint by scavenging inside Residential Containers across any map. It appears specifically during certain map conditions, like an Electromagnetic Storm, Locked Gate, or Night Raid. Alternatively, it can be acquired as a reward from Weekly Trials.

items.name: Antiseptic
items.description: Used to craft medical supplies. Can be recycled into chemicals.
items.article:
Antiseptic is a refined material used to craft medical supplies and upgrading facilities. It is also essential for upgrading your Medical Lab within your Hideout.

Raiders mainly acquire Antiseptic by crafting it at the Refiner. Additionally, it can be found by scavenging the environment and searching containers in medical areas across the map.

items.name: Anvil Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft an Anvil - Has high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
items.article:
The Anvil Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Anvil I hand cannon. Once you have it, this blueprint also allows you to upgrade it into its improved versions: Anvil II, Anvil III, and Anvil IV. Crafting requires access to a Gunsmith station found in your Hideout.

You can find the Anvil Blueprint by opening Raider Caches and other various containers or you can purchase the weapon itself from Tian Wen for coins.

items.name: Anvil I
items.description: Has high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
items.flavor_text: Very effective against ARC armor plating.
items.article: The Anvil I is a hand cannon that uses ammunition. It is effective for hitting targets at medium range, providing strong damage and high headshot damage, though it has a slow firing speed. Raiders can find it by scavenging in the environment or craft it at a Gunsmith after learning the Anvil Blueprint. It can also be purchased from Tian Wen for coins.

items.name: Anvil II
items.description: Has high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
items.flavor_text: Very effective against ARC armor plating.
items.article: The Anvil II is an improved version of the Anvil I hand cannon, which delivers high damage, especially with headshots, and is effective at medium range. It uses heavy ammo. This upgraded version offers a faster firing rate and increased durability compared to its base model, making it more effective in combat. You can craft it at the Gunsmith using an existing Anvil I.

items.name: Anvil III
items.description: Has high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
items.flavor_text: Very effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Anvil III is an upgraded hand cannon that improves upon the Anvil II model. It uses heavy ammo and is designed for high damage, particularly with headshots at medium range. While it maintains a slow handling speed, this version boasts a 50% increased fire rate and better shot accuracy, making it more effective in combat. Raiders obtain it by upgrading an Anvil II at the Gunsmith.

items.name: Anvil IV
items.description: Has high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
items.article: The Anvil IV is the most advanced version of the Anvil hand cannon, firing ammunition. It is designed for hitting targets at medium range and delivers high damage, especially with headshots. Compared to earlier versions, it fires faster and recovers its accuracy more quickly after shooting. This hand cannon is acquired by upgrading an Anvil III at the Gunsmith. To begin crafting the line, you first need to find an Anvil Blueprint, which can be looted from containers.

items.name: Aphelion Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft an Aphelion Rifle
items.article: This blueprint allows Raiders to craft the Aphelion Rifle at a Workbench, provided they have achieved the required Gunsmith bench level. It is known for firing high-velocity energy rounds in two-round bursts. You can find it pretty commonly in the Stella Montis map.

items.name: Aphelion Rifle
items.description: Fires high velocity energy rounds.
items.article:
The Aphelion is a two-round-burst Battle Rifle designed for fighting ARCs. It fires energy rounds and uses ammunition.

To obtain the Aphelion, you first need to acquire its blueprint, which can be found in the Stella Montis map. Once you have it, it can be crafted at a Gunsmith. Additionally, it may be earned as a reward for completing the Furtive Meetings quest.

items.name: Apricot
items.description: A sun ripe apricot. Can be consumed for a small amount of stamina.
items.article:
The Apricot is an uncommon fruit that gives you a small boost of stamina when consumed. It also plays a role in training your Scrappy companion.

You can find Apricots by harvesting them directly from Apricot trees, which are recognized by their green and yellow leaves and small size. When you interact with a tree, it can drop several Apricots. They also commonly spawn on the ground beneath these trees. Additionally, you might discover them by scavenging inside wicker baskets. They are often found on the Blue Gate map.

items.name: Arcade Duck
items.description: For some reason, it feels oddly nostalgic.

items.name: ARC Alloy
items.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities, or by recycling certain ARC parts. Used to craft components.
items.article:
ARC Alloy is a versatile material essential for crafting various components and useful items, helping Raiders advance their gear and complete important projects.

Raiders primarily obtain ARC Alloy by looting arcs and scavenging their remains. It can also be acquired by recycling salvage. Once obtained, it is used at crafting stations to create items. It is also required for progressing through different project stages in your Hideout.

items.name: ARC Circuitry
items.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Used to craft components. Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.
items.article: ARC Circuitry is a rare component essential for crafting and repairing gear. You can obtain it by defeating various ARCs such as the Baron Husk, Bastion, Courier, Matriarch, Probe, Queen, Rocketeer, and Surveyor. It can also be crafted at the Refiner or salvaged from items.

items.name: ARC Conductive Coupler
items.description: One of three distinct couplers found in ARC machines, said to combine into a singular conduit.

items.name: ARC Coolant
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: ARC Coolant is a resource found by salvaging defeated ARCs. It is a specific type of coolant, different from Impure ARC Coolant or standard Coolant. You can obtain it by defeating various ARCs such as the Comet, Fireball, Matriarch, Pop, Queen, Sentinel, Surveyor, and Vaporizer.

items.name: ARC Data Module
items.description: A secondary data module found in a range of ARC machines.

items.name: ARC Flex Rubber
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: ARC Flex Rubber is a rare material that Raiders can recycle to obtain crafting resources. It is obtained by defeating various ARCs across different maps.

items.name: Archive Desk Lamp
items.description: May be worth a few coins.

items.name: ARC Insulated Coupler
items.description: One of three distinct couplers found in ARC machines, said to combine into a singular conduit.

items.name: ARC Motion Core
items.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Used to craft components. Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.
items.article:
The ARC Motion Core is a rare item used to craft various components and upgrade your facilities. It is essential for upgrading your Refiner.

You can get ARC Motion Cores through these methods:

  • By defeating various Bastion, Courier, Leaper, Matriarch, Probe, Queen, Rocketeer, Sentinel, Surveyor, and Turbine.

  • By crafting it at the Refiner.

items.name: ARC Performance Steel
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: ARC Performance Steel is a component used for crafting various items and progressing in certain Expedition Projects. It is obtained by defeating various ARCs found across different maps. Common sources include ARCs such as Arc Probe, Arc Husk, Baron Husk, and Arc Courier. These are frequently encountered in the Blue Gate map, the Dam Battlegrounds map, and the Spaceport map. Additionally, it can be acquired during specific world events like Electromagnetic Storms or Husk Graveyards. This item can also be recycled for resources.

items.name: ARC Plated Coupler
items.description: One of three distinct couplers found in ARC machines, said to combine into a singular conduit.

items.name: ARC Powercell
items.description: Valuable resource that drops from all ARC enemies.
items.article: The ARC Powercell is a common resource used to repair your shields during raids. Using an ARC Powercell restores 20 shield charge over 10 seconds. You can obtain these by defeating any ARCs you encounter, or by scavenging through containers found around the various maps. Additionally, it can be crafted at Workbench, Medical Lab, or by using the In-Round Crafting skill.

items.name: ARC Synthetic Resin
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: ARC Synthetic Resin is a valuable crafting material that helps you complete various projects, such as the Trophy Display project. You can track your progress on projects like this using the Needed Items Tracker. This item is obtained by salvaging it from defeated ARCs. Many different types of ARCs are known to drop this material, including the Baron Husk, Deforester Husk, Hornet, Matriarch, Probe, Queen, Sentinel, Shredder, Snitch, Spotter, Turbine, Turret, and Wasp.

items.name: ARC Thermo Lining
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: ARC Thermo Lining is a material you get from looting arcs. Its main use is to be recycled, which provides valuable crafting resources for your projects. You can obtain it by defeating many different kinds of ARCs, including smaller ones like the Wasp, Tick, Pop, or Fireball, and larger ones such as the Sentinel and Matriarch. But the most reliable way to get this material is to loot Baron Husks and Landing ARC Probes.

items.name: Arpeggio I
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Arpeggio I is an assault rifle that fires in three-round bursts and uses Medium Ammo. It is a balanced weapon with good damage output and accuracy. This weapon can be acquired by finding it while scavenging, or it can be crafted at a Hideout crafting bench with Gunsmith. It serves as the base version, which can be upgraded to the Arpeggio II, then Arpeggio III, and finally the Arpeggio IV. If you no longer need it, the item can be recycled for resources or sold for 5,500 coins.

items.name: Arpeggio II
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Arpeggio II is an upgraded version of the Arpeggio I assault rifle, providing improved combat performance. It fires in three-round bursts and uses Medium Ammo. This upgraded rifle offers a faster firing rate, quicker reloads, and increased durability. Raiders can obtain it by crafting at a Gunsmith workbench in their Hideout. It can also sometimes be found through scavenging while exploring different maps. Like other items, it can be recycled for resources or sold for coins.

items.name: Arpeggio III
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.article: The Arpeggio III is an upgraded three-round-burst assault rifle that offers improved combat performance. It uses medium ammo. This rifle provides a faster fire rate, quicker reloads, and increased durability compared to its previous version, the Arpeggio II. Raiders obtain it by crafting at the Gunsmith.

items.name: Arpeggio IV
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.article: The Arpeggio IV is an advanced assault rifle that fires in three-round bursts and uses medium ammo. It helps Raiders in combat against ARCs by providing a higher fire rate, faster reloading, and better durability compared to its earlier versions. This weapon is crafted from an Arpeggio III at a Gunsmith. Raiders can also sell it for coins or recycle it for salvage.

items.name: Assessor Matrix
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: Assessor Matrix is a specialized part obtained by breaching the ARC Assessor. This unique ARC, a recent arrival, descends from orbit and, guided by ARC Surveyors, lands in pre-set places on the map spawning a patrol of flying ARC enemies around it. The ARC Assessor appears during the Close Scrutiny event.

items.name: Assorted Seeds
items.description: A handful of seeds. Celeste might be looking for these.
items.article: Assorted Seeds are resources Raiders can collect and spend. Their main use is to acquire rare items through trade, offering a way to obtain goods that are not typically found during regular raids in the various maps.

items.name: Aviator (Outfit)
items.description: Aviator outfit is a quest reward from Armored Transports.
items.article: The Aviator (Outfit) is an outfit used to customize your character's appearance in the game. Raiders can obtain this outfit by successfully completing a specific raid. Please note that the exact raid required to unlock it has changed over time.

items.name: Bag (Radio Renegade Variant)
items.description: Radio Renegade Bag Variant - Unlock by completing Power Out Quest.
items.article: The Bag (Radio Renegade Variant) is a backpack that helps you carry more items during your raids. You can obtain this bag by successfully completing the Power Out quest. Once unlocked, it allows you to bring more resources and supplies back to your Hideout.

items.name: Banana (Backpack Charm)
items.description: Banana backpack charm from Medical Merchandise quest.
items.article: This is a banana-themed backpack charm. Its primary purpose is to serve as an item required for the Medical Merchandise quest. Raiders obtain it as part of their progress within this quest. It has no weight.

items.name: Bandage
items.description: A medical item that gradually restores health over time.
items.article: A Bandage is a medical item used to gradually restore your health over a short period. It helps you recover from damage while out in the field. You can obtain a Bandage by scavenging it from containers or the environment. It can also be crafted at a Medical Lab or a Workbench. If you have the In-Round Crafting skill, you can even craft one during a raid. Additionally, you can purchase one from Lance for 750 coins.

items.name: Banjo
items.description: A playable banjo used to attract ARC's attention, and impress other Raiders.

items.name: Bantam Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Bantam

items.name: Bantam I
items.description: Short-barrel revolver with varied fire rate, good handling and damage, but with low accuracy, control and range.

items.name: Bantam II
items.description: Short-barrel revolver with varied fire rate, good handling and damage, but with low accuracy, control and range.

items.name: Bantam III
items.description: Short-barrel revolver with varied fire rate, good handling and damage, but with low accuracy, control and range.

items.name: Bantam IV
items.description: Short-barrel revolver with varied fire rate, good handling and damage, but with low accuracy, control and range.

items.name: Barricade Kit
items.description: A deployable cover that can block incoming damage until it breaks.
items.flavor_text: Health: 500
items.article: The Barricade Kit is a deployable utility item designed to provide temporary cover during raids. Once placed, it creates a wall-like structure that blocks incoming damage, and it can be taken down for reuse. This kit also serves as a surface for placing other defensive tools, such as Laser Traps. Raiders can find it by scavenging or by crafting at the Utility Station. A vendor named Apollo sometimes sells this item for coins.

items.name: Barricade Kit Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Barricade Kit
items.article: The Barricade Kit Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to craft a Barricade Kit at a utility station. It creates a wall-like structure that offers deployable cover, helping to block incoming damage during engagements. These kits can also be dismantled and redeployed. This blueprint is primarily obtained by looting Electrical Style containers across all maps.

items.name: Basic Camera
items.description: A simple little camera that gets the job done.

items.name: Bastion Cell
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Bastion Cell is a rare ARC component dropped by a defeated Bastion. It is primarily used to upgrade the Gear Bench, as a turn-in item for the Settled in Full quest and more recently as one of the barter items with Nomadic Traders for account upgrades. Raiders obtain this item by salvaging it from Bastions. Like other components, it can be recycled for valuable resources.

items.name: Battered Paperback
items.description: Filled with dog-eared pages and coffee stains, an inquisitive mind may find wisdom nonetheless.

items.name: Battery
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into scrap metal.
items.article:
A Battery is a common crafting component used to create various items, fulfill After Rain Comes, and progress through different project stages in your Hideout.

You can find Batteries by searching common containers and interactive panels such as Recording Panels, Oscilloscopes, and Control Consoles across all maps. They are also obtained by salvaging or recycling salvage. Celeste also sells Batteries for coins.

Batteries are used for crafting items at various stations, including the Workbench, Explosives Station, and Gear Bench. You can also recycle them for resources.

items.name: Beam Resonance Tech
items.description: The Equalizer is at its best when the beam stays exactly where the target would rather not have it. Maybe we can work with that.

items.name: Bent Clothes Hanger
items.description: If you encounter a matching set, consider yourself lucky.

items.name: Bettina Blueprint
items.description: Has slow fire rate and high damage output.
items.article: The Bettina Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Bettina I assault rifle at a Gunsmith bench. This fully-automatic rifle is known for its relatively slow fire rate and high damage output. It also provides the ability to upgrade it into its improved versions: Bettina II, Bettina III, and Bettina IV.

items.name: Bettina I
items.description: Has slow fire rate and high damage output.
items.flavor_text: ARC Armor Penetration: Strong
items.article: The Bettina I is a fully-automatic assault rifle that uses Heavy Ammo. It features a slow firing rate but delivers high damage, making it effective for combating various types of ARCs. This weapon can be crafted at the Gunsmith in your Hideout after you have learned the Bettina Blueprint and gathered the necessary components. Alternatively, you may find it by scavenging during your raids.

items.name: Bettina II
items.description: Has slow fire rate and high damage output.
items.article: The Bettina II is an upgraded version of the Bettina I assault rifle, designed for combat encounters. It provides improved fire rate, faster reloading, and increased durability compared to its base model. Raiders can obtain it by upgrading a Bettina I at a Gunsmith, turning it into a more effective weapon for tackling tougher ARCs. Further upgrades can turn it into the Bettina III and then the Bettina IV.

items.name: Bettina III
items.description: Has slow fire rate and high damage output.
items.article: The Bettina III is a fully-automatic assault rifle that uses heavy ammo. It is a refined version of the base Bettina I, providing Raiders with a weapon for combat against ARCs that offers an increased fire rate, a faster reload speed, and more durability. Raiders obtain this weapon by upgrading a Bettina II through crafting. The initial Bettina I can be either scavenged or crafted after its blueprint has been learned.

items.name: Bettina IV
items.description: Has slow fire rate and high damage output.
items.article: The Bettina IV is an upgraded, fully-automatic assault rifle used in combat, firing heavy ammo. This version provides a 15% increased fire rate and 33.3% reduced reload time compared to the Bettina III. Raiders obtain it by upgrading at the Gunsmith.

items.name: Bicycle Pump
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: A Bicycle Pump is a tool that can be recycled for resources or used to complete specific quests, such as The League. You can find this item by scavenging the environment. A reliable way to obtain a Bicycle Pump is by interacting with a bicycle on the Buried City map. It is often found in similar spots to the Deflated Football, which is also part of The League quest.

items.name: Binoculars
items.description: A basic pair of binoculars with two levels of magnification.
items.article:
The Binoculars are a gadget that lets you look at distant areas with two levels of zoom. They are helpful for scouting ahead or taking pictures. You can find these by scavenging them in the game world, or craft them at a Utility Station. They are also sold by Shani for 20 coins. Additionally, you can receive three of them from the "SCOUT PACK" found on Page 1 of the Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager.

COMPLIANT

items.name: Bison Driver
items.description: A critical control component from a Bison vehicle.
items.article: The Bison Driver is a control component salvaged from a type of vehicle called a Bison. This item is valuable for Raiders seeking to gain resources or coins, as it can be recycled. To acquire it, Raiders must defeat ARCs.

items.name: Black Eye (Face Style)
items.description: Maintain at least Rookie III rank in trials until season end.
items.article: The Black Eye (Face Style) is a cosmetic item that lets you change how your Raider's face looks. This item helps you personalize your character's appearance. Raiders can obtain this face style by achieving and maintaining at least a Rookie III rank in Weekly Trials until the season concludes. It was available during Trials Season 2.

items.name: Black (Hiker Colour)
items.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection for the Hiker backpack
items.flavor_text: COSMETIC - Hiker Colour
items.article: The Black (Hiker Colour) is a cosmetic item that changes the appearance of your Hiker backpack to a black color, adding a new style option to your collection. The specific way to obtain it is not commonly found from looting arcs, looting containers, or within standard maps. This suggests it may have been a special or limited-time reward.

items.name: Black & White (Origin Color)
items.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection. Complete Off the Radar Quest.
items.article: The Black & White (Origin Color) is a cosmetic item used to personalize your character's appearance. Adding this item to your collection unlocks a new visual style, offering a black and white coloration option for outfits. You can obtain this cosmetic by successfully completing the Off the Radar quest.

items.name: Blaze Grenade
items.description: A grenade that detonates on impact, covering an area in fire that deals damage over time.
items.article: The Blaze Grenade is a throwable item that bursts into flames on impact, creating a fiery area. This area of fire deals damage over time to any ARCs caught within its radius. You can craft this item at an Explosives Station level 1 once you have learned the Blaze Grenade Blueprint. It can also be scavenged from the environment.

items.name: Blaze Grenade Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Blaze Grenade
items.article: The Blaze Grenade Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft Blaze Grenades at an Explosives Station or Workbench. These grenades are throwable items that explode upon hitting a surface, leaving behind an area of fire that burns and damages ARCs for a short period. You can find it by scavenging throughout different areas as you explore.

items.name: Blaze Grenade Trap
items.description: A laser trip wire that detonates a Blaze Grenade.
items.article: The Blaze Grenade Trap is a deployable device that projects a visible red laser tripwire. When the laser is interrupted, the trap detonates, igniting the surrounding area. This causes fire damage over time to any ARCs or Raiders caught in the flames. You can place these traps on most surfaces, and an undetonated trap can be disarmed and recovered by the Raider who placed it. Raiders can obtain Blaze Grenade Traps through scavenging, possibly with the "One Raider's Scraps" skill, or by crafting them at a Workbench with the "Traveling Tinkerer" skill.

items.name: Bloated Tuna Can
items.description: Something tells you that you don't want to open this...
items.article: The Bloated Tuna Can is a consumable item designed to help your raider quickly recover stamina. When used, it provides a noticeable boost to your stamina bar, allowing you to sprint longer, climb more effectively, or perform other actions without interruption. You primarily obtain Bloated Tuna Cans by searching and looting containers found throughout commercial and residential areas within the various maps.

items.name: Blown Fuses
items.description: Scorched and useless. The burnt metal smells faintly like Apollo's workshop.

items.name: Blue Gate Cellar Key
items.description: Unlocks certain cellar doors near the Blue Gate
items.article: The Blue Gate Cellar Key is a special item used to unlock specific cellar doors found throughout the Blue Gate map. Using this key allows Raiders to access otherwise locked areas, which often contain resources or provide alternative paths. Raiders can obtain this key by exploring various parts of the map, frequently in the vicinity of the cellars it opens.

items.name: Blue Gate Communication Tower Key
items.description: Unlocks a door by the Communication Tower near the Blue Gate
items.article: The Blue Gate Communication Tower Key is used to unlock a specific room in the basement of Pilgrim's Peak, found within the Blue Gate map. Accessing this room can provide Raiders with useful resources. Raiders obtain this key by searching various containers located throughout the Blue Gate map, such as server racks, weapon boxes, drawers, and resource crates.

items.name: Blue Gate Confiscation Room Key
items.description: Unlocks a door to the confiscated goods area within the Blue Gate tunnels
items.article: The Blue Gate Confiscation Room Key is a key used to unlock the Confiscation Room within the Blue Gate map. Opening this room allows Raiders to access various items and resources.

items.name: Blue Gate Village Key
items.description: Unlocks a door to one of the old Village buildings near the Blue Gate
items.article: The Blue Gate Village Key is a key specifically designed to unlock a particular door in the Blue Gate map. Raiders use this key to access restricted areas, such as a village cellar or other locked buildings within the area. This key serves a similar purpose to other access items like the Patrol Car Key or Dam Testing Annex Key, which are also used to open specific doors in different locations. Its utility lies in providing entry to key locations.

items.name: Blue Light Stick
items.description: A throwable chemical light that illuminates the area around it.
items.flavor_text: Illumination Radius 7m
items.article: The Blue Light Stick is a throwable item that illuminates the surrounding area with a blue light for 40 seconds within a 7-meter radius. It helps Raiders see in dark spaces, providing visibility during raids. Raiders can obtain this item through scavenging from various containers found across maps, or by crafting it at a Utility Station after learning the required Blue Light Stick Blueprint. It can also be purchased from the vendor Apollo.

items.name: Blue Light Stick Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Blue Light Stick.
items.article: The Blue Light Stick Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a Blue Light Stick. To use it, select it and choose "Learn and Consume" while in Speranza, your personal hub. This blueprint is obtained by searching Electrical Containers, which are found on any map. It can also be acquired as a reward from Trials.

items.name: Blue (Radio Renegade Color)
items.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection. Complete the Switching the Supply Quest.
items.article: The Blue (Radio Renegade Color) serves as a cosmetic customization option. It allows Raiders to modify the visual style of the Radio Renegade outfit by applying a blue color scheme. Details on how to acquire this specific color variation are not included in the provided information.

items.name: Blue Yellow (Aviator Color)
items.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection.
items.article: The Blue Yellow (Aviator Color) is a cosmetic option that changes the appearance of your Aviator (Outfit), adding a blue and yellow color scheme. You can obtain this cosmetic variant by completing the Armored Transports quest.

items.name: Bobcat Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Bobcat I
items.article: The Bobcat Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Bobcat I submachine gun at a Gunsmith Bench in your Hideout, assuming you meet the crafting requirements. It is generally obtained by participating in specific in-game events such as Locked Gate or lately by searching First Wave Caches during the Hurrican Map Condition.

items.name: Bobcat I
items.description: Has high fire rate but low accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Bobcat I is a fully-automatic Submachine Gun (SMG) that uses light ammo. It is known for its fast firing rate, though it has lower accuracy compared to other weapons. This weapon is used to deal damage to ARCs during encounters.

Raiders can obtain the Bobcat I by finding it as loot while scavenging in different maps, or by crafting it at the Gunsmith once the Bobcat Blueprint is learned.

items.name: Bobcat II
items.description: Has high fire rate but low accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Bobcat II is an upgraded model of the Bobcat I, a fully-automatic submachine gun. This version offers several practical improvements for Raiders, including a tighter shot pattern, less horizontal pushback when firing, quicker reloading, and increased durability. To obtain it, Raiders must upgrade their existing Bobcat I at a Gunsmith.

items.name: Bobcat III
items.description: Has high fire rate but low accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Bobcat III is an enhanced version of the Bobcat II submachine gun, offering significant improvements for combat. As a fully-automatic weapon, it utilizes ammunition to engage ARCs. This version features increased firing control due to reduced shot dispersion and horizontal recoil, making it more reliable in sustained engagements. Additionally, it benefits from a faster reload time and greater overall durability. Raiders can acquire it by upgrading a Bobcat II at a Gunsmith station.

items.name: Bobcat IV
items.description: Has high fire rate but low accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Bobcat IV is the final upgraded version of the Bobcat I, a fully-automatic submachine gun that uses light ammo. This advanced variant significantly improves the weapon's control by reducing shot spread and horizontal recoil, along with faster reloads and increased durability. It can be found by scavenging or by crafting it at a Gunsmith after learning the Bobcat Blueprint.

items.name: Bombardier Cell
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Bombardier Cell is a component salvaged from Bombardiers. It helps Raiders progress by serving as a material for various upgrades and projects. You need it to upgrade the Refiner, which is used for crafting. These cells are also a requirement for the Expedition 3 project and the Trophy Display project, which contribute to your overall progression or Hideout improvements. Bombardier Cells are obtained by defeating Bombardiers, a type of ARC commonly found in Buried City as well as most other maps. This item can also be recycled for valuable resources.

items.name: Bow and Arrow (Emote)
items.description: Emote is rewarded for maintaining at least a Wildcard III rank in trials until the season end.
items.article: The Bow and Arrow (Emote) is a cosmetic item that allows your character to perform a gesture of aiming and firing an imaginary bow. This emote is rewarded to Raiders who maintain at least a Wildcard III rank in Weekly Trials until the end of a season.

items.name: Breathtaking Snow Globe
items.description: The envy of every Speranzan. Proof that this world was once thriving and magical.
items.article: The Breathtaking Snow Globe is a Trinket. It showcases a tiny Cold Snap, a visual effect from Raider's Refuge. This item is primarily used as a requirement for 'Expedition 3 Stage 4' of a project. You obtain it by scavenging within specific areas, such as Residential, Old World, or Commercial zones, which can be found across various maps.

items.name: Briefcase (Backpack Attachment)
items.description: Maintain at least Tryhard III rank in Trials until the season end.
items.article: The Briefcase (Backpack Attachment) is a cosmetic item that changes the visual appearance of a Raider's backpack. It attaches to the bottom of the backpack, displaying a small briefcase. This attachment does not affect gameplay or Raider abilities. It was available as a reward for Raiders who achieved at least the Tryhard III rank during Trials Season 1.

items.name: Broken Compass
items.description: A broken compass, its needle fixed stubbornly in one direction. An odd choice of gift.

items.name: Broken Flashlight
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Broken Flashlight is a resource Raiders gather primarily to recycle for materials. It serves as a source of materials needed for various crafting and upgrading projects. You can find this item by scavenging and searching through containers within security areas.

items.name: Broken Guidance System
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Broken Guidance System is a component Raiders gather to complete specific projects and objectives. It serves as a component in crafting. Raiders primarily obtain this item by scavenging and searching containers in areas that feature industrial structures. This item can also be recycled for various resources.

items.name: Broken Handcuffs
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: Broken Handcuffs are an uncommon item that Raiders collect in the game. Their primary use is to be recycled, providing useful crafting resources needed to upgrade your tools and weapons or craft new items at the Workbench. You will typically find these handcuffs when searching inside various containers throughout your raids.

items.name: Broken Handheld Radio
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: A Broken Handheld Radio is a salvageable item that Raiders collect primarily to be recycled. This process provides crafting materials, which are essential for creating new gear or upgrading existing items at various workbenches in the Hideout. Raiders commonly obtain this item through scavenging, finding it within containers or as environmental loot, particularly in areas described as Security zones across the different maps.

items.name: Broken Taser
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Broken Taser is a resource that Raiders can acquire and recycle to gain general crafting materials. It helps you progress by providing resources needed for various crafting and upgrading projects at a Workbench. You can typically find it by looting containers or scavenging the environment within areas described as security zones or buildings.

items.name: Bronze Statuette
items.description: An aged but beautiful bronze statuette. Rumor has it that the Nomad Envoy collects these.

items.name: Bruiser (Backpack)
items.description: White

items.name: Bully Fragmenter
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

items.name: Bureau Desk Lamp
items.description: May be worth a few coins.

items.name: Burgerboy (Backpack Charm)
items.description: Burgerboy backpack charm from Into The Fray quest.
items.article: The Burgerboy (Backpack Charm) is a cosmetic item used to personalize your Raider's backpack. This charm serves a decorative purpose, allowing Raiders to customize the look of their gear. You can obtain it as a reward for completing the Into the Fray quest.

items.name: Buried City Hospital Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Hospital in Buried City
items.article:
The Buried City Hospital Key is used to unlock a specific door on the second floor of the Hospital in the North West corner of the Buried City map. This room often contains useful items.

Raiders can find this key by scavenging it from containers or other lootable spots within Buried City. It is also given as a reward for completing the Life of a Pharmacist quest.

items.name: Buried City JKV Employee Access Card
items.description: Unlocks a door in the J Kozma Ventures company building in Buried City
items.article: The Buried City JKV Employee Access Card is a keycard that grants entry to specific JKV employee rooms found throughout the Buried City map. These rooms often contain various items and supplies helpful for your expeditions. Raiders typically obtain this access card by exploring the Buried City. It serves a similar role to the Buried City Residential Master Key, which opens other locked areas in the same location.

items.name: Buried City Residential Master Key
items.description: Unlocks certain apartment doors in Buried City
items.article: The Buried City Residential Master Key is a key used to open specific doors found within the Buried City map. These doors allow access to new areas or reveal additional resources. Raiders primarily obtain this key by looting arcs such as the Surveyor, which are encountered while exploring the map.

items.name: Buried City Town Hall Key
items.description: Unlocks the door to the Town Hall in Buried City
items.article: The Buried City Town Hall Key is a key item specifically designed to unlock the main entrance of the Town Hall building in the Buried City map. Finding this key allows Raiders to access the Town Hall building, which is otherwise inaccessible and may contain valuable items or progress quests. Raiders typically obtain this key by thoroughly exploring the Buried City map, searching various containers and hidden spots in the environment.

items.name: Burletta Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Burletta
items.article: The Burletta Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Burletta pistol. The specific way to acquire this blueprint is often a topic of discussion among Raiders, as it does not currently exist as a drop in the game. The Burletta blueprint is strictly a Quest Reward. You must complete the “Industrial Espionage” questline from Tian Wen in Speranza to receive it as a Reward.

items.name: Burletta I
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Burletta I is a semi-automatic pistol that uses Light Ammo. It functions as a useful sidearm for Raiders to deal damage against ARCs. This pistol can be acquired in a few ways: Raiders might find it while scavenging, craft it at the Gunsmith once they have the Burletta Blueprint (which is given as a reward for completing the Industrial Espionage project), or buy it from the vendor Tian Wen.

items.name: Burletta II
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Burletta II is an upgraded version of the Burletta I pistol, designed for improved performance in combat. This semi-automatic pistol offers a faster reload speed along with increased durability compared to its previous iteration. Raiders obtain it by crafting at a Gunsmith.

items.name: Burletta III
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Burletta III is a version of the semi-automatic Burletta pistol that uses light ammo. It serves as an upgraded weapon, offering a 33.3% faster reload time and an additional 20 durability points compared to the Burletta II. This item is obtained by crafting it at a Gunsmith bench.

items.name: Burletta IV
items.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Burletta IV is the highest-tier upgrade of the Burletta I semi-automatic pistol, which uses light ammunition. This improved version offers 50% reduced reload time and increased durability compared to the base model. Raiders obtain it by upgrading a Burletta III at the Gunsmith. It can be salvaged, crafted after acquiring its Burletta Blueprint (a reward from the Industrial Espionage quest), or purchased from Tian Wen.

items.name: Burned ARC Circuitry
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: Burned ARC Circuitry is an uncommon item. Its main purpose is to be recycled for crafting materials. This item, which appears damaged, was originally a functional ARC Circuitry. Raiders can find it by scavenging the remains of ARCs.

items.name: Burnt-out Candles
items.description: After the grid fell candles became the preferred source of light for many. Unlike electricity, a good old candle will never fail you. Unless it's windy. Or raining. Or...
items.article: Burnt-Out Candles are a Trinket. As a Trinket, this item functions primarily as a collectible resource for Raiders. Raiders can find and acquire Burnt-Out Candles by scavenging the environment. These items are typically located in specific zones, such as the Residential and Old World areas. When no longer needed, they can be recycled for additional resources.

items.name: Burst Assembly Recovery
items.description: Shredders manage rapid volleys with little downtime. Careful dismantling with a Raider Tool might preserve the firing assembly long enough to figure out how.

items.name: Cable Stripper
items.description: Used in crafting.

items.name: Calculator
items.description: Used in crafting.

items.name: Camera Lens
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Camera Lens is a component you can recycle to get resources. You can find this item by searching containers such as Lockers and areas labeled Security Breach. It is commonly found while exploring the Buried City map, the Dam Battlegrounds map, and the Stella Montis map. You can also discover it in the Blue Gate map and The Spaceport map.

items.name: Candleberries
items.description: A waxy berry that grows only during a small window each year. People have depended on them to make candles, foods and medicine for ages.
items.article: Candleberries are a waxy berry, classified as a nature item, that grow only during a small window each year. They are used to progress through the Flickering Flames event. You can obtain Candleberries by harvesting them directly from Candleberry bushes. These bushes only appear when the Cold Snap Cold Snap modifier is active. Additionally, you can find them by scavenging during the Cold Snap. This item can be recycled for resources.

items.name: Candle Holder
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Candle Holder is an uncommon item found throughout the world. Its main purpose is to be recycled for crafting materials, which are useful for various building projects or upgrades. You can typically find Candle Holders by looting residential containers in specific areas. Look for them in the Pale Apartments and Ruby Residence within the Dam map. They are also present in Plaza Rosa and the Grandioso Apartments in the Buried City map.

items.name: Canister
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into plastic.
items.article: The Canister is an uncommon topside material used as a crafting component for a variety of items. Raiders can obtain Canisters by scavenging in commercial areas within the map. They are also sold by Celeste with a daily purchase limit. Additionally, Canisters can be acquired by recycling salvage.

items.name: Cans (Backpack Attachment)
items.description: A set of cans that are a backpack attachment from the quest Safe Passage.
items.article: The Cans (Backpack Attachment) is a cosmetic item you can use to customize the appearance of your Raider's backpack. This item attaches to the bottom of your backpack, adding a visual detail that moves as your Raider does. It is obtained by completing the Safe Passage quest.

items.name: Canto Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Canto SMG.
items.article: The Canto Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to craft the Canto, a fully-automatic submachine gun, at a Gunsmith. This blueprint is found by opening First Wave Caches.

items.name: Canto I
items.description: Fully automatic submachine gun with a larger caliber.
items.article: The Canto I is a fully-automatic submachine gun that uses medium ammo, providing a fast rate of fire for combat. It can be found inside First Wave Caches, or you can craft it after learning the Canto Blueprint at a Gunsmith workbench.

items.name: Canto II
items.description: Fully automatic submachine gun with a larger caliber.
items.article: The Canto II is an upgraded version of the Canto I submachine gun. It provides Raiders with an improved weapon that features reduced shot dispersion, an increased magazine size, faster reload times, and greater durability. Raiders obtain it by upgrading a Canto I at a Gunsmith workbench, which can typically be found in the Hideout.

items.name: Canto III
items.description: Fully automatic submachine gun with a larger caliber.
items.article: The Canto III is an upgraded version of the Canto submachine gun that uses Medium Ammo. It offers better accuracy, a larger magazine capacity, faster reload times, and increased durability compared to the Canto II. Raiders can obtain it by upgrading one at a crafting station.

items.name: Canto IV
items.description: Fully automatic submachine gun with a larger caliber.
items.article: Canto IV is the final upgraded version of the Canto submachine gun. It provides enhanced combat performance with 45% reduced maximum shot dispersion, an additional 6 rounds in its magazine, 43% faster reload time, and 30 more points of durability. Raiders can craft this improved weapon at a Gunsmith by upgrading a Canto III.

items.name: Caposta (Outfit)
items.description: Mask

items.name: Cat Bed
items.description: At least a tiny bit more comfortable than your face.
items.article: The Cat Bed is a Trinket item. Its main use is as a component for upgrading certain equipment at the Workshop. Raiders can obtain Cat Beds by scavenging them from containers and lootable spots found in commercial and residential areas.

items.name: Celeste's Journal
items.description: Battered and torn, you can see the faint outline of doodles along the edges.

items.name: Cheer (Emote)
items.description: Cheer Emote - Quest reward from The Right Tool
items.article: The Cheer (Emote) is a cosmetic item that lets your character perform a specific animation to express themselves. It provides a non-verbal way for Raiders to show enthusiasm, agreement, or celebrate moments with their teammates during raids. This emote is exclusively obtained as a reward when you complete the quest titled 'The Right Tool'.

items.name: Chemicals
items.description: Used to craft medical supplies, explosives, and utility items.
items.article:
Chemicals are a basic material used for crafting various items. They are also required for certain workshop upgrades and projects.

Raiders primarily find Chemicals by scavenging in Mechanical, Residential, and Medical areas across all maps. They are often found in containers like cars and bags. Popular maps for finding Chemicals include the Blue Gate and Spaceport. You can also get Chemicals from events such as Harvester and Night Raid, purchase them from Celeste at the Dam Battlegrounds, or obtain them by recycling other items.

items.name: Coffee Pot
items.description: The power to face a new day, one drip at a time.
items.article: The Coffee Pot is a trinket used to progress the "Expedition 3" project, specifically Stage 3. Raiders obtain this item by looting residential containers. These containers are commonly found in the Pale Apartments and Ruby Residence areas within the Dam Battlegrounds map. It can also be found in the Plaza Rosa E Apartment and Grandioso Apartments of the Buried City map.

items.name: Coins
items.description: Used to buy gear from Traders. Earned by selling loot and completing quests.
items.article: Coins are a fundamental type of in-game money that Raiders earn and use in ARC Raiders. They are essential for acquiring various items, services, and upgrades that contribute to your overall strength and progression. Raiders primarily obtain them by successfully completing raids. You can gather large amounts of coins from these activities to support your efforts against the ARCs.

items.name: Colorful Shoes
items.description: This specialized footwear is adorned with vibrant ceremonial designs, and designed to anchor the wearer to the ground. It is thought to have belonged to ancient wanderers of great renown.

items.name: Colorful Shoes
items.description: This specialized footwear is adorned with vibrant ceremonial designs, and designed to anchor the wearer to the ground. It is thought to have belonged to ancient wanderers of great renown.

items.name: Colorful Shoes
items.description: This specialized footwear is adorned with vibrant ceremonial designs, and designed to anchor the wearer to the ground. It is thought to have belonged to ancient wanderers of great renown.

items.name: Combat Mk. 1
items.description: Basic combat augment. Supports stronger shields, but with limited backpack capacity and Quick Use slots.
items.article: The Combat Mk. 1 is an augment that allows you to equip a medium shield, which provides more defense during your raids. In exchange for this increased protection, this augment reduces the number of items you can carry in your backpack and limits your quick-use slots. You can get this augment by exchanging a Free Loadout Augment with Lance, crafting it at a Gear Bench, or by sometimes finding it while scavenging items.

items.name: Combat Mk. 2
items.description: A combat augment more focused on maneuverability than absorbing damage.
items.flavor_text: Restores 1 health every 5 seconds. When damage is taken, the effect is paused for 30 seconds.
items.article: The Combat Mk. 2 is a Combat augment that serves as a direct upgrade to the Combat Mk. 1. This augment focuses on helping with maneuverability and provides a passive health regeneration of 1 health every 5 seconds. Taking damage will pause this health regeneration effect for 30 seconds. It also increases your available backpack slots and weight capacity, and offers compatibility with Light, Medium, and Heavy Shield types, along with one dedicated grenade slot. Raiders can craft this augment at a Gear Bench.

items.name: Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive)
items.description: An improved version of the Combat II augment. Supports more shield types, and comes with extra space for grenades.
items.flavor_text: Restores 2 health every 5 seconds. When damage is taken, the effect is paused for 30 seconds.
items.article: The Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive) is an augment that builds upon the Combat Mk. 2, offering an upgraded passive ability. It provides passive health restoration, healing 2 health every 5 seconds, with the healing pausing for 30 seconds after taking damage. This augment also expands a Raider's options by supporting light, medium, and heavy shield types, and offers additional space for grenades. It can be crafted at a Gear Bench using the corresponding blueprint.

items.name: Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive) Blueprint
items.description: An improved version of the Combat II augment. Supports more shield types and comes with extra space for grenades
items.article: The Combat Mk.3 (Aggressive) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive) augment at a Gear Bench. This augment improves upon the Combat Mk. 2 by offering compatibility with more shield types and providing extra space for grenades. When equipped, it also helps restore your health over time. It can be found as loot throughout the world, often discovered in containers or obtained after looting arcs across different maps.

items.name: Combat Mk. 3 (Flanking)
items.description: A combat augment more focused on maneuverability than absorbing damage.
items.flavor_text: Stowed or unequipped Pistols and Hand Cannon are 33% faster to equip.
items.article: The Combat Mk.3 (Flanking) is an augment that helps you move around more easily during combat. It specifically allows you to equip stowed or unequipped Pistols and Hand Cannons 33% faster, which can be helpful for quick weapon swaps. This augment is compatible with light and medium shields. You can obtain it either by scavenging in the environment or by crafting it at Gear Bench using a blueprint.

items.name: Combat Mk. 3 (Flanking) Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Combat Mk. 3 (Flanking)
items.article: The Combat Mk. 3 (Flanking) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to create the Combat Mk. 3 (Flanking), a special gear piece that enhances your combat abilities. This particular augment focuses on maneuverability, letting you equip stowed pistols and hand cannons 33% faster. It is designed to work with both light and medium shields. To acquire it, you must first find this blueprint by scavenging during your raids, and then use it at a Gear Bench to craft the item.

items.name: Comet Igniter
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Comet Igniter is a throwable item that explodes after a short delay, dealing damage to anything nearby. Its main use is to help clear out groups of Comets or deal area damage during encounters. You can craft it at an Explosives Station. Raiders obtain this item by scavenging destroyed Comets, but only if the Comet did not explode on its own. It can also be recycled for resources.

items.name: Compact Combustion Charges
items.description: Most explosives end with the detonation. Blaze Grenades have the good sense to keep causing trouble afterward. There may be something worth borrowing in that.

items.name: Compensator I
items.description: Slightly reduces per-shot dispersion.
items.flavor_text: 10% Reduced Max Shot Dispersion
items.article: A Compensator I is a type of weapon modification that helps reduce how much your shots spread out when you fire your weapon.

items.name: Compensator II
items.description: Moderately reduces per-shot dispersion.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest

items.flavor_text: 20% Reduced Max Shot Dispersion
items.article: The Compensator II is a weapon modification that helps your shots spread out less, making your aim more consistent. This modification can be found by scavenging during your raids, or you can purchase it directly from Shani for 100 coins, with a daily limit of two. Alternatively, if you have the Compensator II Blueprint, you can craft it at a Gunsmith.

items.name: Compensator II Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Compensator II
items.article: This blueprint allows Raiders to craft the Compensator II, a weapon mod that helps reduce bullet spread when firing. Raiders can find it by scavenging during raids, often inside Residential Containers. It can also be earned as a reward from Weekly Trials. Additionally, Raiders can purchase it from Shani for 100 coins, with a limit of two per day. Once learned, this blueprint is consumed and unlocks the crafting recipe at a Gunsmith Bench.

items.name: Compensator III
items.description: Significantly reduces per-shot dispersion.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest

items.flavor_text: 30% Reduced Max Shot Dispersion
items.article: The Compensator III is a weapon modification that primarily reduces how much your shots spread out and also lessens the maximum spread of your shots. This item also causes your weapon's durability to drain faster. You can craft it at the Gunsmith bench level 1.

items.name: Compensator III Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Compensator III
items.article: The Compensator III Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Compensator III at a Gunsmith Bench. This modification helps reduce how much your shots spread out when you fire quickly, and also lessens the overall maximum spread of your shots. It does cause your weapon to lose durability faster.

items.name: Complex Gun Parts
items.description: Used to craft advanced weapons.
items.flavor_text: Used to craft: Equalizer, Aphelion, Jupiter
items.article:
Complex Gun Parts are components used to craft advanced weapons.

You can obtain them through general scavenging or by defeating certain ARCs, including specific types like the Queen and Matriarch. They can also be crafted at a Refiner once you have learned the complex gun parts blueprint. Additionally, these parts can be purchased from Celeste for 60 coins, with a limit of one per day.

items.name: Complex Gun Parts Blueprint
items.description: Used to craft advanced weapons.
items.article: The Complex Gun Parts Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft Complex Gun Parts at a Refiner. These are then used with other blueprints at a Gunsmith to craft weapons.

items.name: Coolant
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: Coolant is a rare item that can be recycled for crafting materials. This item is different from Impure ARC Coolant and ARC Coolant.

items.name: Cooling Coil
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: A Cooling Coil is a component used in various projects. For example, it is required for stage 2 of the Expedition 2 project. To find Cooling Coils, search inside containers and environmental objects like car hoods, buses, mobile generators, metal crates, car tool cabinets, industrial drawers, and red lockers, which are often found in industrial areas.

items.name: Cooling Fan
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Cooling Fan is a rare item used in crafting projects. It serves as a component for the Expedition 1, Stage 2 project. Beyond crafting, you can recycle this item to gain crafting materials. Raiders obtain it primarily through scavenging. Look for Cooling Fans inside Server Racks, which are often found within specific rooms that hold various types of loot across different maps.

items.name: Cracked Bioscanner
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Cracked Bioscanner is a component used to upgrade the Medical Lab to Medical Lab. It can also be recycled for resources.

items.name: Crash Mat
items.description: A throwable emergency landing device, to soften some heavy landings.
items.article: The Crash Mat is a throwable item that deploys an inflatable mat on the ground. Its primary purpose is to soften heavy landings and reduce fall damage when you fall onto it. You can obtain it by crafting at a Utility Station after you have learned the Crash Mat Blueprint.

items.name: Crash Mat Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Crash Mat

guide_links.label: How to Find Crash Mat Blueprint

items.article: The Crash Mat Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to craft a Crash Mat at the Utility Station. It is a throwable item that creates an inflatable mat, which you can fall onto to reduce damage from heavy landings.

items.name: Crimson Racer (Aviator Colour)
items.description: Crimson Racer (Aviator Colour) is a quest reward from Communication Hideout
items.article: The Crimson Racer (Aviator Colour) is a cosmetic item Raiders receive as a reward for completing a specific task. Its main role is to mark progress through the game's quests. Raiders obtain this item by finishing the Communication Hideout quest.

items.name: Crude Explosives
items.description: Used to craft explosives. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article:
Crude Explosives are throwable items that create a loud noise and a small explosion. They can be crafted at a Refiner.

These explosives are typically found by searching industrial loot containers such as Metal Crates. You can find these crates in locations like the Research and Administration west tunnels or the Power Generation Complex in the Dam Battlegrounds map, and the Shipping Warehouse in the Spaceport map. Additionally, they can be salvaged from defeated Pop and Fireball ARCs.

items.name: Crumpled Plastic Bottle
items.description: Can be recycled into plastic parts.
items.article: The Crumpled Plastic Bottle is an uncommon item. Raiders typically find these bottles while scavenging in residential areas. Its primary purpose is for recycling, where it provides useful resources.

items.name: Damaged ARC Motion Core
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Damaged ARC Motion Core is a broken version of an ARC Motion Core. While no longer intact, it is useful for its raw components. Its primary purpose is to be recycled at a workbench or similar station to obtain crafting materials, which help you make new gear or upgrade existing items. Raiders can obtain this item by defeating specific ARCs, such as the Baron Husk and the Courier, and then salvaging parts from their defeated husks.

items.name: Damaged ARC Powercell
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: A Damaged ARC Powercell is a component primarily used to obtain resources through recycling. Raiders can get this item by defeating various ARCs, such as the Courier and the Husk, which are commonly encountered in the Dam Battlegrounds map. Recycling it provides useful materials and coins.

items.name: Damaged Fireball Burner
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: A Damaged Fireball Burner is a common used item that once functioned as a Fireball Burner. Its primary purpose is to be recycled for crafting materials. You can obtain this item by salvaging defeated Fireballs. Additionally, it can be retrieved from the ground after a Fireball Burner has been thrown and used.

items.name: Damaged Heat Sink
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Damaged Heat Sink is a rare item that helps you improve your base. Its main purpose is to upgrade the Utility Station, making it more effective for your operations. You can also recycle this item to obtain crafting resources. You can find Damaged Heat Sinks by scavenging while exploring maps.

items.name: Damaged Hornet Driver
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Damaged Hornet Driver is a common item that provides crafting materials when recycled. It is a worn-out version of a Hornet Driver. Raiders can find it by scavenging the remains of defeated Hornets, or by collecting a Hornet Driver after it has been thrown during gameplay.

items.name: Damaged Leaper Pulse Unit
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

items.name: Damaged Rocketeer Driver
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Damaged Rocketeer Driver is a component obtained by scavenging the remains of defeated ARCs, specifically from Rocketeer Husks. This item was previously a complete Rocketeer Driver before being damaged. You can recycle it to acquire crafting materials.

items.name: Damaged Snitch Scanner
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

items.name: Damaged Tick Pod
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Damaged Tick Pod is a damaged pod that was once an intact Tick Pod. Its primary use is to be recycled, providing valuable crafting materials for various needs. Raiders typically obtain this item by scavenging the husks of Ticks.

items.name: Damaged Wasp Driver
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Damaged Wasp Driver is a common item used as a resource for crafting. You can recycle it to obtain materials for your projects. This item is found by defeating specific ARCs, such as the Wasp and other enemy types. These ARCs are frequently encountered throughout the Dam Battlegrounds map.

items.name: Dam Controlled Access Zone Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Controlled Access Zone on Dam Battlegrounds.
items.article: The Dam Controlled Access Zone Key is a key that grants entry to the Controlled Access Zone, a specific area located within the Dam Battlegrounds map. Entering this zone often presents Raiders with a button puzzle to solve. In some cases, tackling this puzzle may involve multiple Raiders coordinating their efforts, potentially utilizing tools such as a snap hook.

items.name: Dam Control Tower Key
items.description: Unlocks a door to the Control Tower on Dam Battlegrounds.
items.article: This key opens a specific locked door, providing access to a hidden or restricted area, such as a control tower, located within the Dam map.

items.name: Dam Staff Room Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Research and Administration building on Dam Battlegrounds.
items.article: The Dam Staff Room Key is used to unlock a specific door within the Research and Administration building, located on the first floor of the Dam Battlegrounds. Gaining access to this locked area helps Raiders progress or find useful items. This key can be obtained by scavenging the map or by completing the Tribute To Toledo quest.

items.name: Dam Surveillance Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Water Treatment Control building on Dam Battlegrounds.
items.article: The Dam Surveillance Key is a key used to open a locked door. This key unlocks a room found on the first floor, on the south side of the Water Treatment buildings in the Dam Battlegrounds. Raiders can obtain this key by scavenging around the map, or by completing the Greasing Her Palms quest.

items.name: Dam Testing Annex Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Testing Annex on Dam Battlegrounds.
items.article: The Dam Testing Annex Key is a key used to open locked doors inside the Testing Annex building on the Dam Battlegrounds map. There are two locked doors on the ground level of the Testing Annex, one on the south side and one on the east. You will need one key for each door you wish to unlock. This key is awarded for completing the A Lay Of The Land quest. You can also find it by scavenging in containers like lockers, drawers, and filing cabinets within the map.

items.name: Dam Utility Key
items.description: Location is currently unknown except that it is on Dam Battlegrounds.
items.article: The Dam Utility Key is a key used to unlock a specific area or container within the Dam Battlegrounds map. You can obtain this key by scavenging and looting containers found across the Dam Battlegrounds map. Additionally, it is given as a reward for completing the Flickering Threat quest.

items.name: Dart Board
items.description: Some Raiders use it to practice dexterity. Others just like throwing things at other things.
items.article: The Dart Board is a trinket that your Raider has not yet found a way to use for a practical purpose. Some Raiders use it to practice their aiming, while others simply enjoy throwing things at it. You can find this item by scavenging in commercial and residential areas.

items.name: Dead Flowers
items.description: Don't give these to your date.

items.name: Deadline
items.description: A mine that deals damage to anything within its radius once the timer runs out.
items.article:
The Deadline is an explosive mine that Raiders can deploy, which detonates after a fixed 6-second timer. Once its timer runs out, it causes a large explosion that damages anything caught within its blast radius. After being placed, the mine cannot be disarmed or picked up before it explodes.

Raiders can find the Deadline by scavenging or craft it at an Explosives Station once they have learned the Deadline Blueprint. It is also sold by Apollo for 18,000 coins, with a limit of one per day.

items.name: Deadline Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Deadline Mine
items.article: The Deadline Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to craft a Deadline. It is a mine you can place that explodes after a fixed 6-second timer, dealing damage to anything nearby. You can buy this blueprint from Apollo for 18,000 coins; he sells one per day. Once learned, you can craft it at an Explosives Station level 1.

items.name: Defibrillator
items.description: An injection that quickly revives downed raiders and restores some health.
items.article:
A Defibrillator is a healing item that quickly brings a downed Raider back into action, restoring more health than a standard revive. It helps your team stay in the fight longer by getting allies back on their feet faster.

You can craft this item at Medical Lab once you have learned the Defibrillator Blueprint. It is also available for purchase from Lance for 3,000 coins. Additionally, you might find it in a Free Loadout or as part of various Raider Decks, such as AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager, AR/RD 002: Goalie, and AR/RD 003: Surgeon.

items.name: Defibrillator Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Defibrillator
items.article: The Defibrillator Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a healing item at a Medical Lab. It is used to quickly revive downed Raiders and restore some of their health. This blueprint can be bought from Lance for 3,000 coins.

items.name: Deflated Football
items.description: Just by looking at this, you too start to feel slightly deflated.
