items.description: A standard magazine does its job, but it can only hold so much. Getting familiar with a drum-fed design could reveal how that extra room is put to use, and where the same idea might fit elsewhere.

items.name: Magnet
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article:
A Magnet is a common component used to create various items. You can find Magnets through general scavenging in the environment or purchase them from Celeste.

Raiders can also obtain Magnets by recycling salvage. Additionally, you can salvage them into crafting materials.

items.name: Magnetic Accelerator
items.description: Used to craft advanced weapons.
items.article:
The Magnetic Accelerator is a refined component used in crafting and repairing advanced weapons. It also serves as a key material for various projects.

You can obtain Magnetic Accelerator by looting arcs such as the Queen. It can also be found through scavenging in the game world.

This item is crafted at a Refiner, requiring salvage materials. Additionally, it can be recycled for other crafting materials.

items.name: Magnetron
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Magnetron serves as a crafting material. You can recycle it to obtain other resources needed for crafting. This item is also a requirement for the Snap And Salvage quest, where you'll need one Magnetron in addition to a Flow Controller. You can find it by scavenging throughout the Stella Montis map.

items.name: Major Aiva's Mementos
items.description: A closely-shut box, covered in many years worth of dust.

items.name: Major Aiva's Patch
items.description: A torn patch, found amidst rubble and ruin.

items.name: Marano Market Business Card
items.description: The scribbled writing on this business card almost obscures the logo of Marano's market.

items.name: Mask Fragment
items.description: Half a face, cast in bronze.

items.name: Mastery Medal (Backpack Charm)
items.description: Maintain Wildcard I trials rank until the season end.
items.article: The Mastery Medal (Backpack Charm) is a cosmetic item you can attach to your Raider's backpack. It hangs from the bottom and swings as your Raider moves, allowing you to customize your character's look. This charm is obtained by maintaining the Wildcard I rank in Trials until the season ends.

items.name: Matriarch Reactor
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.flavor_text: Used to Craft: Aphelion
items.article: The Matriarch Reactor is a component salvaged from defeated Matriarchs. It is used in crafting advanced weapons and can also be traded for account upgrades with Ermal - the Nomadic Envoys Trader.

items.name: Mechanical Components
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article:
Mechanical Components are a refined material used to craft, repair, and upgrade a variety of items, especially weapons. They are also essential for upgrading the Gunsmith.

You can obtain Mechanical Components by scavenging in the environment or by defeating specific ARCs like the Bastion, Bombardier, Leaper, and Shredder. Additionally, you can craft them at the Refiner by combining salvage materials.

items.name: Medium Ammo
items.description: Medium bullets used mainly with medium-caliber weapons. Such as Rattler, Tempest, Arpeggio, Renegade and Torrente.
items.article:
Medium Ammo is a type of ammunition used by weapons that fire medium-caliber rounds. It performs better at penetrating ARC armor than light ammo, but is not as effective as heavy ammo.

Raiders can obtain Medium Ammo by looting arcs like the Bastion and Hornet, or by scavenging it from Raider Caches. It can also be crafted at the Workbench, or purchased from Tian Wen.

items.name: Medium Gun Parts
items.description: Assorted spare parts used for rifles.
items.article: Medium Gun Parts are assorted spare parts used to upgrade, craft, and repair weapons. You can find these parts by scavenging through containers and environmental loot, or by looting Bastion and Sentinel ARCs. Additionally, they can be crafted at the Refiner once you have learned the Medium Gun Parts Blueprint, using salvage. Celeste also offers a daily limited stock of these parts. If you have surplus, they can be recycled for other resources.

items.name: Medium Gun Parts Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft Medium Gun Parts
items.article: The Medium Gun Parts Blueprint is a blueprint that allows Raiders to craft medium gun parts at the Refiner. These parts are a resource used in various crafting projects, primarily for building and upgrading weapon components.

items.name: Medium Shield
items.description: A standard shield that blocks a medium portion of incoming damage at a moderate cost to mobility.
items.article:
The Medium Shield is a standard shield that provides Raiders with a fair amount of protection by blocking incoming damage, at the cost of a small reduction to movement speed. It is a versatile defensive option for various situations.

Raiders can obtain the Medium Shield through several methods: by scavenging in the environment, from Raider Caches, or as an item from Raider Decks. It can also be purchased from Lance for 6000 coins, with a daily limit of three. Additionally, it can be crafted at a Gear Bench.

To equip this shield, Raiders must have one of the following Augments installed:

  • Combat Mk. 1

  • Tactical Mk. 1

  • Combat Mk. 2

  • Tactical Mk. 2

  • Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive)

  • Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper)

  • Looting Mk. 3 (Survivor)

  • Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive)

  • Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing)

items.name: Metal Brackets
items.description: Can be recycled into metal parts.
items.article: Metal Brackets are an uncommon component item. They can be recycled to obtain crafting materials.

items.name: Metal Parts
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items.
items.article: Metal Parts are a common material used to craft a wide range of items. You can find them by searching containers and environmental objects like metal crates, car hoods, server racks, and seed vaults. This material can also be obtained by recycling salvage or by purchasing them from Celeste.

items.name: Microscope
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Microscope is a rare item primarily used to gain various crafting materials and coins when recycled. This item is found by searching containers across different areas, most reliably within the Stella Montis map. It appears frequently during the Night Raid event.

items.name: Mini Centrifuge
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Mini Centrifuge is designed to be recycled for crafting materials. Its main purpose is to provide resources that help with Raider progression and projects. You can find this item by scavenging the environment throughout Stella Montis. Upon recycling, it yields various crafting materials and other components.

items.name: Mini Pump
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

items.name: Mobile-Fire Grip Fittings
items.description: Fast movement is useful right up until a weapon needs to come into play. A weapon that keeps up with the pace would be useful.

items.name: Mod Components
items.description: Used to craft weapon mods. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: Mod Components are refined materials used to craft various weapon modifications. Raiders typically obtain them by crafting at the Refiner using other components, or by recycling salvage. Once acquired, they are essential for creating advanced weapon mods at the Gunsmith Bench.

items.name: Moisture Meter
items.description: Measures soil moisture levels for precise irrigation control.

items.name: Moss
items.description: Can be used to regain a small amount of health.
items.article: Moss restores a small amount of health over ten seconds when consumed. It is also used to craft medical supplies. You can obtain Moss by harvesting it from dead trees and inside Hydroponic Domes in the Dam Battlegrounds. It can also be found in Wicker Baskets or purchased from Celeste for 10 coins, with a daily limit of 5. If not needed for crafting or healing, it can be recycled into other resources.

items.name: Motor
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: A Motor is a mechanical component used for workbench upgrades. Its primary purpose is to help improve your Hideout by upgrading the Refiner. You can find Motors by scavenging from containers, often within car hoods in the Water Treatment area of the Dam Battlegrounds. Motors can also be recycled into general crafting materials.

items.name: Mountaineer's Detector
items.description: Useful for finding foreign objects hidden in the snow. As an added bonus, it works just as well on sand.

items.name: MRI Duck
items.description: Has technology gone too far?

items.name: Mushroom
items.description: Can be consumed to regain a small amount of health.
items.article:
Mushrooms are a healing item you can consume to recover a small amount of health. They are also used to train Scrappy.

You can find Mushrooms in various places across several maps. In the Dam Battlegrounds map, look for them on pipes in the Water Treatment Control area, along the sandy shores and inside irrigation planters of the Hydroponic Dome Complex, and on nearby trees in the Central Swamp Lift and Wreckage areas. In the Spaceport map, check the small hangar south of the East Container Yard, on a tree there, and inside underground tunnels in the center of the map. In the Riven Tides map, they grow on trees in the Dried Riverbed. They can also be found inside wicker baskets during the Lush Bloom minor map condition.

items.name: Music Album
items.description: Perfect for relaxing nights at home, casual get-togethers, and private air guitar concerts.
items.article: The Music Album is a collectible item related to the game's soundtrack. Raiders may find a use for these albums as they can be utilized for various projects.

items.name: Music Box
items.description: Worth a small fortune.
items.article: The Music Box is a collectible item primarily valued for its sell price. It can be safely sold for coins, serving as a reliable way to gain coins. It is similar to other collectible items like the Painted Box, Playing Cards, and Poster of Natural Wonders.

items.name: Muzzle Brake I
items.description: Slightly reduces both vertical recoil & horizontal recoil.
items.flavor_text: 15% Reduced Horizontal Recoil
items.article: Muzzle Brake I is a weapon modification used to improve weapon handling. It helps reduce how much your weapon kicks up or moves sideways when you fire, making it easier to aim and hit your targets more consistently.

items.name: Muzzle Brake II
items.description: Moderately reduces both vertical recoil & horizontal recoil.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest

items.flavor_text: 20% Reduced Horizontal Recoil
items.article:
The Muzzle Brake II is a weapon modification used to improve your aim by reducing how much your weapon moves when fired. It provides a moderate reduction in both how much your gun kicks upwards and how much it moves to the sides. This helps make your shots more consistent.

You can craft this modification at a Gunsmith station. To do so, you will first need its blueprint and crafting materials. It can also be recycled to recover basic resources.

items.name: Muzzle Brake II Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Muzzle Brake II
items.article: The Muzzle Brake II Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Muzzle Brake II weapon modification at a Gunsmith Bench level 2 to reduce a weapon's vertical and horizontal recoil. Blueprints like this are commonly found by scavenging in containers such as Raider Containers. They can also be acquired as rewards from Weekly Trials or Quests.

items.name: Muzzle Brake III
items.description: Significantly reduces both vertical recoil & horizontal recoil.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest

items.flavor_text: 25% Reduced Vertical Recoil Control - 25% Reduced Horizontal Recoil Control
items.article: The Muzzle Brake III is a weapon modification. It reduces both vertical and horizontal recoil by 25% each, helping you keep your weapon steady while firing. This mod also causes your weapon to use up its durability 20% faster. You can craft this item at a Gunsmith bench level 1 after acquiring the Muzzle Brake III Blueprint.

items.name: Muzzle Brake III Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Muzzle Brake III
items.article: The Muzzle Brake III Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Muzzle Brake III at a Gunsmith Bench. This item is a weapon modification that helps reduce how much your weapon kicks up (vertical recoil) and swings side-to-side (horizontal recoil) when you fire it.

items.name: Noisemaker
items.description: A deployable proximity sensor that sounds an alarm when enemy Raiders are detected.
items.flavor_text: Trigger Radius 8m
items.article:
The Noisemaker is a deployable gadget that acts as a proximity sensor. When placed, it triggers an alarm for 4 seconds if enemy ARCs enter its 8-meter detection range, helping you stay aware of nearby threats. This item can be attached to most surfaces.

You can get a Noisemaker by scavenging the environment or crafting it if you have the Traveling Tinkerer skill. It is also sold by Apollo for 1,920 coins, with a daily limit of 6. Additionally, you can find ten of these in the Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager. Five are included in the MAYHEM PACK, and another five in the PROTECTION PACK.

items.name: Number Plate
items.description: Can be recycled into metal parts.
items.article: The Number Plate is an uncommon item. Its primary use is for recycling, where it breaks down into general crafting materials.

items.name: Nutrient Meter
items.description: Ideal for monitoring soil and water nutrient levels in greenhouses or fields.

items.name: Official Shutdown Documentation
items.description: Top-secret protocols outlining the shutdown of Project Heartwood.

items.name: Oil
items.description: Used to craft weapons and explosives. Can be recycled into chemicals.
items.article: Oil is a versatile crafting material used to craft items at workbenches. It is also a necessary resource for completing certain quests and progressing through larger projects. You can find Oil by scavenging containers and structures across the different maps. Additionally, it can be obtained by recycling salvage or by purchasing it from the vendor Celeste.

items.name: Old World Books
items.description: The past survives in fragments, often dull or ordinary, yet priceless to the right person.

items.name: Olives
items.description: Can be consumed for a small amount of stamina.
items.article: Olives are a consumable item that quickly restores 20 stamina when eaten. You can find Olives by harvesting them from Olive Trees. Look for these trees in places like the Olive Grove in the Blue Gate map. You might find 1 to 4 olives on the ground under a tree, or you can interact with the tree directly to make them drop. Olives also appear when scavenging inside Wicker Baskets. Beyond quick stamina recovery, they can be used in training. They can also be recycled for other resources.

items.name: Orange Camo (Origin Outfit)
items.description: Orange camo color is unlocked for completing The Trifecta quest.
items.article: The Orange Camo (Origin Outfit) unlocks a specific orange camouflage pattern for your character's outfit. This cosmetic item allows you to customize your appearance. You can obtain this outfit color by completing The Trifecta quest.

items.name: Osprey Blueprint
items.description: Has reliable damage output and accuracy.
items.article: The Osprey Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to construct the Osprey I sniper rifle. It enables creation of improved versions, letting you upgrade an Osprey I to an Osprey II, then to an Osprey III, and finally to an Osprey IV. Crafting the initial Osprey I requires a Gunsmith skill level of 2, while upgrading to subsequent tiers requires a Gunsmith skill level of 1.

items.name: Osprey I
items.description: Has reliable damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Osprey I is a bolt-action sniper rifle designed for hitting targets from long distances, featuring a built-in scope. It uses Medium Ammo. You can craft this item at a Gunsmith Bench level 1 after learning the Osprey Blueprint. It can be upgraded into more advanced versions, including the Osprey II, Osprey III, and Osprey IV.

items.name: Osprey II
items.description: Has reliable damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Osprey II is an upgraded sniper rifle, building upon the Osprey I to provide better performance in long-range engagements. This bolt-action rifle uses medium ammo and features a scope for precise targeting. It offers quicker bolt action and faster reloading times, alongside increased durability. Raiders can craft it at a Gunsmith by upgrading an Osprey I with other components.

items.name: Osprey III
items.description: Has reliable damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Osprey III is an advanced version of the Osprey II sniper rifle, maintaining its role as a reliable long-range weapon that uses medium ammo. This upgraded rifle provides better combat efficiency by significantly reducing the time it takes to cycle the bolt and reload. It also features improved durability, allowing for more sustained use before needing repairs.

Raiders obtain the Osprey III by upgrading an Osprey II at a Gunsmith Bench. After obtaining it, the rifle can be further improved at a Gunsmith Bench or recycled for salvage.

items.name: Osprey IV
items.description: Has reliable damage output and accuracy.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Osprey IV is the top-tier Osprey sniper rifle. This scoped, bolt-action weapon uses medium ammo, excelling at precise, long-range shots with reliable damage against ARCs. It offers improved handling, faster reload, and enhanced durability compared to previous versions. You craft it at the Gunsmith Bench level 1 by upgrading an Osprey III. It can be recycled for resources or repaired.

items.name: Padded Stock
items.description: Significantly improves stability.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Arpeggio, Bettina, Rattler, Kettle, Ferro

items.flavor_text: 15% Reduced Horizontal Recoil - 30% Reduced ADS Speed
items.article:
The Padded Stock is a weapon modification that makes your weapon more stable. It helps reduce how much your weapon moves when you shoot (recoil) and makes your shots land closer together (dispersion). Equipping this modification will also slightly increase the time it takes to ready your weapon, put it away, and aim down sights.

You can get the Padded Stock through a few methods:

  • It can be found by scavenging in the environment.
  • You can craft it at a Gunsmith if you have the Padded Stock Blueprint and other necessary crafting materials.
  • It can be purchased from Tian Wen for 15,000 coins, with a limit of one per day.

items.name: Padded Stock Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Padded Stock
items.article: The Padded Stock Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Padded Stock weapon modification at a Gunsmith Bench. This modification improves weapon stability by reducing vertical and horizontal recoil, and also lessens how much your shots spread. However, it slightly increases the time it takes to ready your weapon or aim down sights. You can obtain this blueprint by looting various containers in Residential areas as well as looting Surveyor ARCs.

items.name: Painted Box
items.description: May be worth a few coins.
items.article: The Painted Box is a resource in ARC Raiders. No specific details are available regarding its purpose or how it is obtained.

items.name: Patchwork (Warden Color)
items.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection.
items.article: Patchwork (Warden Color) is a cosmetic variant that adds a new color option to your Warden outfit. Raiders can obtain this item by completing a quest from Shani.

items.name: Patrol Car Key
items.description: Unlocks the rear door of a patrol car
items.article: The Patrol Car Key is a key that can be used to open a patrol car.

items.name: Patrol (Outfit)
items.description: Rewarded for maintaining at least  a Daredevil I rank in the trials until the season ends.
items.article: The Patrol outfit is a cosmetic item that changes the appearance of your character. Raiders can earn this outfit by participating in and achieving ranks in the Weekly Trials.

items.name: Pendola Pass Observatory Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Cielo Sereno Observatory main building on Pendola Pass.

items.name: Pendola Pass Old Town Key
items.description: Unlocks a door to an apartment in the Old Town on Pendola Pass.

items.name: Pendola Pass Railyard Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Controlled Receiving Facility on Pendola Pass.

items.name: Pendola Pass Train Station Key
items.description: Unlocks a door in the Almatera Station on Pendola Pass.

items.name: Photoelectric Cloak
items.description: A gadget that allows the user to conceal themselves from ARC.
items.article:
The Photoelectric Cloak is a gadget that lets you temporarily hide from ARCs. When you use it, ARCs will lose sight of you, even if you were already fighting them. While cloaked, you can only move slowly. The cloak uses energy, which is shown by a meter on your screen. This energy slowly refills once the cloak is no longer active, even if you put it away. Using the cloak consumes a small amount of energy immediately, so it is often better to use it for longer periods rather than short bursts.

You can craft this item at a Utility Station. It can also be obtained as a reward from specific projects, such as the Trophy Display (Stage 2) or Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie (Page 4). Additionally, it can be recycled to recover materials.

items.name: Pilgrim's Peak Security Code
items.description: Temporary security code to unlock the main gate.
items.flavor_text: Can only be used during Locked Gate
items.article:
The Pilgrim's Peak Security Code is a temporary code used to unlock a main gate on the Blue Gate map. It is essential for opening a specific gate during a 'Locked Gate' map condition, as you need four different codes to fully unlock it.

You can find this code inside any lootable container within the Pilgrim's Peak location on the Blue Gate map. At least one code typically appears during a round, and you might find more. To use the code, proceed to the Gate Control Room on the Blue Gate map, enter the building, and submit it at one of the four terminals. Submitting a code consumes it and activates the terminal which helps to open the Locked Gate.

items.name: Planks
items.description: Used in crafting.

items.name: Plastic Parts
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items.

items.name: Plastic Trash
items.description: Can be recycled into plastic parts.

items.name: Playing Cards
items.description: Speranzans love to see who can build the tallest tower - before the tremors knock them down.
items.article: Playing Cards are rare individual items that can be collected. They have a certain value and can be sold for coins within the Crafting Materials & Misc item category.

items.name: Pneumatic Actuator
items.description: Used to craft amplified weapons.

items.name: Polluted Air Filter
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Polluted Air Filter is a filter Raiders can recycle for crafting materials. Raiders can find this item by scavenging through different areas described as industrial.

items.name: Pop Trigger
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

guide_links.label: Destroy Ticks, Fireballs and Pops: Weekly Trial

items.article:
The Pop Trigger is an uncommon deployable item that rolls forward and creates a small explosion after a short delay. It is used to upgrade your Explosives Station, craft the Fireworks Box, and contribute to projects like the Trophy Display. You can also recycle Pop Triggers for crafting materials.

You can find this item by scavenging defeated Pop and Courier ARCs.

items.name: Portable TV
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: A Portable TV is a decorative item that can be recycled for crafting materials. It is also used as a requirement for the Movie Night quest. You can find Portable TVs by scavenging in the Buried City map, often located in dressers in residential areas or sometimes on couches and chairs in archive sections.

items.name: Possibly Toxic Plant
items.description: A speculated source of miraculous healing, and/or particularly nasty rashes.

items.name: Poster of Natural Wonders
items.description: If you stand close and squint your eyes, it's like the world never came crumbling down.
items.article: A Poster of Natural Wonder is a decorative item scavenged from the environment. Raiders primarily use this by selling it for coins. It can also be recycled to gain various resources. You can find this by scavenging in commercial and residential areas within the map.

items.name: Potted Plant
items.description: A small but tenacious plant, growing happily in a pot

items.name: Pottery
items.description: May be worth a few coins.
items.article: Pottery is a crafting material that can be sold for coins.

items.name: Power Bank
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Power Bank is a recyclable item used to obtain crafting materials. Raiders can find this item inside containers such as Lockers and Breachable Containers. These are commonly encountered in maps like the Blue Gate, the Stella Montis, and the Dam Battlegrounds. Additionally, it may be found during the Night Raid event. When recycled, it provides various crafting resources and can also be sold for coins.

items.name: Power Cable
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Power Cable is a material primarily used to improve your crafting abilities. It is needed to upgrade your Gear Bench to Gear Bench, a process which also requires other crafting materials. This item can also be recycled into basic crafting materials.

items.name: Powered Descender
items.description: Reduces fall speed when used in the air, but has a wind-up time before reaching full force. Shuts down once out of power.
items.article: The Powered Descender is a gadget that helps you control your fall. When you use it in the air, it slows down your descent, allowing you to land safely. It needs a moment to fully activate and will stop working when it runs out of power. You can craft it at a Utility Station after you have learned the Powered Descender Blueprint. You can keep track of blueprints you need with the Needed Items Tracker.

items.name: Powered Descender Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Powered Descender

guide_links.label: How to Find Powered Descender Blueprint

items.article: The Powered Descender Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to craft the Powered Descender at a Utility Station. This gadget reduces your fall speed when you use it in the air, allowing for safer descents. It takes a moment to reach its full effect and will shut down once its power runs out.

items.name: Power Rod
items.description: Used in crafting.
items.article:
The Power Rod is a refined material used to craft various advanced equipment and tools. It is also required for the Tribute To Toledo quest and can open a specific door in the east side of the Power Generation Complex on the Dam Battlegrounds map.

Raiders can obtain a Power Rod by crafting it at the Refiner. It is also a reward for completing the Groundbreaking quest. Additionally, you can acquire it by recycling or salvaging other items.

items.name: Precision Gimbal
items.description: A particularly mesmerizing part, supposedly crucial to the construction of Exodus spaceships.

items.name: Pressure Regulator
items.description: Used to craft amplified weapons.

items.name: Prickly Pear
items.description: Can be consumed for a small amount of stamina.

items.name: Processor
items.description: Used in crafting.
items.article:
The Processor is a crafting component used to make different items. It can also be recycled into other materials.

You can find Processors by searching interactive objects in the environment. It is also obtained by recycling various items. Additionally, Celeste offers a limited supply of Processors for purchase daily.

items.name: Project Heartwood Blueprints
items.description: A mix of complex-looking blueprints and reports, labeled Project Heartwood.

items.name: Projector
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Projector is a rare item that can be broken down into crafting materials. Its main use is to provide resources when recycled, which are essential for crafting. Similar to other components, it helps Raiders gather valuable materials. You can find Projectors by scavenging the environment, typically within residential areas.

items.name: Project Pathos Empathy Core
items.description: A prototype android core said to instill empathy and self-determination in androids.

items.name: Propellant Valve Assembly
items.description: Used to craft amplified weapons.

items.name: Pulse Mine
items.description: A proximity-triggered mine that pops up and knocks back anything within its radius.
items.article:
A Pulse Mine is a device that triggers when an enemy gets close, creating a burst that pushes targets away without causing damage. It is useful for controlling groups of ARCs or creating space during combat.

This item can be crafted at an Explosives Station once you have learned the Pulse Mine Blueprint, using materials obtained through salvage. It is also available for purchase from Apollo for 1,410 coins, with a daily limit of 6.

items.name: Pulse Mine Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Pulse Mine
items.article: The Pulse Mine Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Pulse Mine at an Explosives Station. These are proximity-triggered devices that activate when enemies come near, with a 1-second delay before detonating. Upon detonation, they release a kinetic blast that does not deal damage, but pushes back targets within a 7.5-meter radius. It can be acquired from Apollo for 1,410 coins, with a daily purchasing limit of six.

items.name: Purification System Blueprint
items.description: Detailed plans for assembling a functional purification system.

items.name: Purple Glam (Face Style)
items.description: MakeupGlamPurple

items.name: Queen Reactor
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Queen Reactor is a crafting component primarily used to create weapons and currently commonly used to trade for various account upgrades with Ermal - the Nomadic Envoys Trader. You can use it to craft items at a Gunsmith. Raiders obtain the Queen Reactor by scavenging destroyed Queens or by looting their leg armor segments that break off during battle.

items.name: Radial Press
items.description: Used in crafting.

items.name: Radio
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Radio is a rare item that can be recycled into crafting materials. You can find this item by scavenging in areas described as Commercial and Residential.

items.name: Radio Relay
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Radio Relay is a component that can be processed at a recycling station to obtain salvage materials. You can find Radio Relays by scavenging in the Stella Montis map. Look for them in containers or by searching the general environment.

items.name: Radio Renegade (Outfit)
items.description: Radio Renegade outfit is given to you as a reward from the quest Switching The Supply
items.article: The Radio Renegade (Outfit) is an ensemble that customizes your character's look. It allows Raiders to change their appearance in the game.

items.name: Raider Flag
items.description: Sun-bleached and wrinkled, yet dignified all the same.

items.name: Raider Hatch Key
items.description: Unlocks a Raider Hatch.
items.article: The Raider Hatch Key is a key designed to unlock Raider Hatches, providing a way to escape difficult situations on the surface. This key can be found through scavenging or crafted at a Utility Station if you possess the Traveling Tinkerer skill. Additionally, Shani offers this key for sale for 100 coins, with a limit of two per day.

items.name: Raider Logbook
items.description: Surprisingly dilligent notetaking, in surprisingly legible handwriting.

items.name: Raider's Refuge Security Code
items.description: Temporary security code to unlock the main gate.
items.flavor_text: Can only be used during Locked Gate
items.article: The Raider's Refuge Security Code is a temporary code used to unlock the main gate during the "Locked Gate" map condition. You need four of these codes to open the gate. To use a code, go to the Gate Control Room location on the Blue Gate map, enter the building, and submit it at one of the four terminals inside. Submitting a code consumes it and activates the terminal which helps to open the Locked Gate.

items.name: Raider Tokens
items.description: Used to purchase decks and cosmetics.
items.article: Raider Tokens are resources that Raiders use to unlock various rewards and content as they play the game. They are specifically needed to obtain items from what is known as 'free decks,' a system designed to provide Raiders with additional content.

items.name: Railway Lantern
items.description: Once kept trains from running into each other in the dark.

items.name: Rascal
items.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
items.article:
The Rascal is a break-action grenade launcher that uses launcher ammo. It fires explosive projectiles designed to detonate only when they hit ARCs, making it useful for direct combat against ARCs.

Raiders can obtain the Rascal by crafting it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1. The Rascal Blueprint is required to craft the initial Rascal I. It can then be upgraded to more advanced versions, such as the Rascal II, Rascal III, and Rascal IV, by crafting them from the previous version. It can also be recycled for salvage.

items.name: Rascal Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Rascal
items.article:
The Rascal Blueprint is a rare blueprint in ARC Raiders, added in Patch 1.29.0. If you're wondering how to find the Rascal Blueprint in ARC Raiders - it drops from Raider Containers across all maps and requires a Gunsmith Workbench to craft.

Best Ways to Find the Rascal Blueprint:

  • Raider Containers — Weapon Cases, Raider Caches, and Ammo Crates are your best source across all maps.

  • Security Breach Lockers — Breach Lockers scattered across all maps have confirmed drops. Use Metaforge Interactive Maps to find them.

  • Key Rooms — Locked rooms with high loot density can also yield the blueprint as a general drop.

Tips to Maximize Rascal Blueprint Drops: Run Night Raid for boosted rare blueprint drop rates. Safe Pocket the blueprint the moment you find it. Go in naked with items to keep farming runs low-risk.

items.name: Rascal II
items.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
items.article: The Rascal II is an improved break-action grenade launcher. It fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARCs, and uses launcher ammo. This upgraded version provides 7% reduced reload time and an additional 10 durability. Raiders can craft it at a Gunsmith. It can also be found while exploring the Buried City map. When no longer needed, it can be recycled for resources.

items.name: Rascal III
items.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
items.article: The Rascal III is an upgraded break-action grenade launcher that fires explosive projectiles, which detonate only when hitting an ARC. This weapon provides a 13% reduced reload time and an additional 20 durability compared to its previous version. It uses launcher ammo. Craft it at the Gunsmith from a Rascal II and other required components, or recycle it for resources. It can be further upgraded into the Rascal IV.

items.name: Rascal IV
items.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
items.article: The Rascal IV is a further upgraded version of the Rascal, a special break-action grenade launcher. This weapon fires explosive projectiles that detonate only when they hit an ARC, making it suitable for direct combat. It uses Launcher Ammo and offers improved durability and a faster reload time compared to earlier versions. You can craft it at a Gunsmith by upgrading a Rascal III. The initial Rascal weapon requires a Rascal Blueprint to craft before it can be upgraded.

items.name: Rattler I
items.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Rattler I is a fully-automatic assault rifle that uses medium ammo. It is an inexpensive weapon that provides good damage and accuracy for close to medium range encounters.

Raiders can obtain the Rattler I in a few ways:

  • It can be crafted at the Gunsmith.
  • It can be received as part of a Free Loadout.
  • It can also be found through scavenging.

It can be used to craft the Rattler II, or it can be recycled or salvaged for other resources.

items.name: Rattler II
items.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Rattler II is an improved version of the Rattler I assault rifle, designed for Raiders seeking a more reliable combat option. It offers an increased magazine size and better durability compared to its previous version. This weapon fires medium ammo and provides good damage and accuracy for engaging ARCs at close to medium range.

You can craft the Rattler II at a Gunsmith by upgrading an existing Rattler I using salvage.

items.name: Rattler III
items.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Rattler III is an upgraded version of the Rattler II assault rifle, using medium ammo. This fully-automatic weapon offers increased magazine capacity and improved durability, making it a reliable option for various combat situations. You can obtain it by crafting at the Gunsmith Bench. It can also be used as a component to further upgrade to a Rattler IV. Additionally, it can be recycled for various resources or salvaged for materials, or sold for coins.

items.name: Rattler IV
items.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Rattler IV is an advanced version of the Rattler assault rifle, which uses medium ammo. This weapon provides a solid option for fighting ARCs at close to medium range. Compared to its previous versions, it offers an increased magazine size and improved durability.

You obtain the Rattler IV by upgrading a Rattler III at the Gunsmith. This crafting process requires other materials to complete. It can also be recycled for various resources and components.

items.name: Recorder
items.description: A playable recorder used to attract ARC's attention, and impress other Raiders.
items.article: The Recorder is a playable instrument that plays two different melodies. It can be used to attract the attention of ARCs. Other Raiders can join in by playing instruments like the Shaker and Acoustic Guitar. While playing, you cannot perform actions that require both hands.

items.name: Red Coral Jewelry
items.description: Valued for its fine craftsmanship, and effortless ability to make your eyes pop.
items.article: Red Coral Jewelry helps Raiders progress. It is found by opening red lockers located in the Buried City map.

items.name: Red Light Stick
items.description: A throwable chemical light that illuminates the area around it.
items.article: The Red Light Stick is a consumable item that provides light. It is designed for quick use to help Raiders illuminate dark surroundings, improving visibility during exploration or combat. Similar items include the Yellow Light Stick, Green Light Stick, and Blue Light Stick.

items.name: Red Light Stick Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Red Light Stick.
items.article: The Red Light Stick Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the red light stick at the appropriate crafting station.

items.name: Red (Radio Renegade Color)
items.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection.
items.article: The Red (Radio Renegade Color) is a cosmetic item used to apply a red color scheme. It is part of the Radio Renegade style, which can be used to customize the visual appearance of your radio or other parts of an outfit.

items.name: Reinforced Reception Security Code
items.description: Temporary security code to unlock the main gate.
items.flavor_text: Can only be used during Locked Gate
items.article:
The Reinforced Reception Security Code is a temporary security code used to unlock a main gate. It is one of four codes required to open the gate during the "Locked Gate" Blue Gate map condition.

You can find this code in lootable containers, such as bins, located within the Reinforced Reception area on the Blue Gate map. At least one code will appear per round during this condition, and sometimes more.

To use the code, head to the Gate Control Room on the Blue Gate map. Once inside, interact with one of the four terminals. Submitting a code consumes it and activates the terminal which helps to open the Locked Gate.

items.name: Remote Control
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Remote Control is a device used to activate specific functions, which can help you progress through areas or manage objectives. For example, it is used to open or close extraction points, allowing you to secure your salvaged items. You can find this item by searching various containers scattered across the Stella Montis map. If you have extra Remote Controls, they can be recycled into coins and other general crafting materials.

items.name: Remote Raider Flare
items.description: A deployable device that, when manually triggered, launches a Raider Distress Flare.
items.article: The Remote Raider Flare is a deployable item that, when activated, sends a Raider Distress Flare into the sky, which can be used to signal for help or mark a location. You can find this item by scavenging. It can also be crafted at a utility station if you have learned the Remote Raider Flare Blueprint and have the necessary components. Another way to get it is by purchasing it from Apollo for 810 coins. Finally, it can be obtained from the 'Decks: Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager' on Page 1, specifically within the 'MAYHEM PACK'. When no longer needed, it can be recycled for salvage.

items.name: Remote Raider Flare Blueprint
items.description: Allows you to craft the Remote Raider Flare.
items.article: The Remote Raider Flare Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to produce Remote Raider Flares at a Utility Station. A Remote Raider Flare is a deployable tool that, when activated, launches a distress signal into the sky.

items.name: Renegade I
items.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Renegade I is a lever-action battle rifle that uses medium ammo. It offers high damage, accuracy, and increased headshot damage. This rifle is well-suited for medium to long-range encounters, and its accuracy is particularly good when you are crouching and stationary. For a stealthier approach, equipping a Silencer II or better attachment makes its shots quiet. Be aware that reloading the Renegade I is slower because each shell is loaded individually.

Raiders can obtain it in a few ways. It can be found through scavenging. It can also be crafted if you have Gunsmith skill level 3. Additionally, a vendor named Tian Wen sells it for 21,000 coins, with one item available for purchase each day.

items.name: Renegade II
items.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article: The Renegade II is an upgraded battle rifle that uses medium ammo. This version improves upon the original Renegade I by offering an increased fire rate, better durability, and faster accuracy recovery after firing. It is well-suited for fighting at medium to long distances due to its accuracy and high damage when hitting an enemy's head. To obtain it, craft this weapon by upgrading a Renegade I at the Gunsmith bench.

items.name: Renegade III
items.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Renegade III is a lever-action battle rifle that uses medium ammo. It is an upgraded version of the Renegade battle rifle, offering better damage, accuracy, and headshot damage. With moderate ARC Armor Penetration, it is effective in combat against ARCs, particularly in medium to long-range encounters. This weapon also gains increased fire rate and durability compared to the Renegade II. Equipping it with a Silencer II or better can make it suitable for stealth play.

You obtain the Renegade III by upgrading a Renegade II at a Gunsmith bench, which is located in your Hideout. Its durability can be restored using salvage materials.

items.name: Renegade IV
items.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
items.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
items.article:
The Renegade IV is the highest upgraded version of the lever-action Battle Rifle. It features high damage output, good accuracy, and increased headshot damage, making it effective for medium to long-range engagements. When equipped with a Silencer II or better, it can be used for stealth. This rifle uses medium ammo.

You obtain the base Renegade I by scavenging or by purchasing it from Tian Wen. It is crafted at a Gunsmith bench by improving an earlier version. It offers increased fire rate and durability compared to its previous models.

items.name: Research Points
items.description: Research Points are used to craft Blueprints, Designs and to research Weapon Amplification

items.name: Resin
items.description: Can be used to gradually restore a small amount of health over time.
items.article: Resin is a common healing item that helps you by restoring a small amount of health gradually over time, specifically 1 health per second for 10 seconds after use. You can find Resin by scavenging or by looking inside wicker baskets. Currently, its only known general use is to provide coins during the Lush Blooms and Cold Snap map conditions.

items.name: Ripped Safety Vest
items.description: A remnant of a time long lost, when it was fashionable to stand out.
items.article: The Ripped Safety Vest is an Uncommon item primarily used to obtain crafting resources through recycling. Raiders can find this item by scavenging various containers, such as Breachable Containers, standard Containers, and Lockers, located in the Blue Gate and the Dam Battlegrounds map.

items.name: Riven Tides Classified Records Keycard
items.description: Unlocks a door to the Classified Records room in the Port Authority Building at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Classified Records Keycard is used to unlock a door that leads to the Classified Records room. This room is located inside the Port Authority Building on the Riven Tides map. You can obtain this keycard by scavenging for items in containers or exploring the general environment of Riven Tides.

items.name: Riven Tides Crane House Keycard
items.description: Unlocks a door in one of the Crane Houses at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Crane House Keycard is a keycard that opens a locked door in the middle Crane House within the Riven Tides map. Raiders can typically find this keycard by searching various containers. While it is most commonly found in the Riven Tides map, it can sometimes be looted in the Buried City map as well. This item has a value of 100 coins.

items.name: Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 102
items.description: Unlocks the door to one of Panorama Azzurro's many suites at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 102 is a keycard used to open a locked door. Its primary purpose is to grant access to one of the suites located within the Panorama Azzurro area on the Riven Tides map.

items.name: Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 107
items.description: Unlocks the door to one of Panorama Azzurro's many suites at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 107 is a keycard used to open a specific door in the Riven Tides map. Its primary purpose is to unlock one of the suites located within Panorama Azzurro. This item can be obtained through scavenging while exploring the map, often found in relation to a locked gate. It is also awarded upon completing the Battening Down quest.

items.name: Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 113
items.description: Unlocks the door to one of Panorama Azzurro's many suites at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 113 is a key that unlocks a specific door. Its main purpose is to give you access to one of the many suites located in the Panorama Azzurro area of the Riven Tides map. You can find this keycard by searching containers within the map.

items.name: Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 205
items.description: Unlocks the door to one of Panorama Azzurro's many suites at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 205 is a keycard used to open a specific locked door. Its primary purpose is to unlock one of the suites located at Panorama Azzurro in the Riven Tides map. Raiders can obtain this item by searching various containers found within the Riven Tides map.

items.name: Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 208
items.description: Unlocks the door to one of Panorama Azzurro's many suites at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 208 is a keycard that opens the door to Suite 208 in the Panorama Azzurro hotel. This hotel is found on the Riven Tides map. Obtaining this keycard allows Raiders to access the specific suite. It can be found by scavenging within the Panorama Azzurro hotel area.

items.name: Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 311
items.description: Unlocks the door to one of Panorama Azzurro's many suites at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 311 is a keycard designed to unlock a specific door within the Panorama Azzurro building located on the Riven Tides map. Its primary function is to grant Raiders access to one of the suites found in this area.

items.name: Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 404
items.description: Unlocks the door to one of Panorama Azzurro's many suites at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Hotel Keycard No. 404 is a keycard used to open a specific suite within the Panorama Azzurro area on the Riven Tides map, allowing Raiders to access the locked room.

items.name: Riven Tides Secure Storage Keycard
items.description: Unlocks a door to the Secure Storage room in the Port Authority Building at Riven Tides.
items.article: The Riven Tides Secure Storage Keycard is a keycard that opens a locked door to the Secure Storage room, which is located within the Port Authority Building in the Riven Tides map. Gaining access to this room allows Raiders to find items inside. You can obtain this keycard by searching containers, especially Breachable Containers, which are found across various maps. Raiders have reported finding it most often in the Buried City map, but also in the Dam Battlegrounds map, Spaceport map, Stella Montis map, and Blue Gate map. It is also available during the Night Raid event.

items.name: Rocketeer Driver
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

guide_links.label: Damage Rocketeers, Leapers or Bastions: Weekly Trial
Damage Flying ARC Enemies: Weekly Trial

items.article: The Rocketeer Driver is a component obtained by defeating Rocketeers and scavenging their husks. It is used at the Explosives Station level 3 to craft a ranged weapon. Additionally, multiple Rocketeer Drivers are required for Stage 4 of a Trophy Display project. Raiders can also recycle it for general crafting materials.

items.name: Rocket Thruster
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Rocket Thruster is a rare item that can be recycled into various crafting materials. You can find this item by scavenging in specific areas, such as the Rocket Assembly zones within the Stella Montis map and the Spaceport map.

items.name: Rock Salt
items.description: Decorative, not dinner.

items.name: Roots
items.description: May be worth a few coins.
items.article: Roots are a crafting material used in various projects in ARC Raiders. They can commonly be found under trees and around bushes as well as valleys near broken trees. Check various Metaforge Maps to see where players are finding Roots more commonly.

items.name: Rope
items.description: Used in crafting.
items.article: Rope is a rare crafting material. You can use it at a Utility Station to craft utility items. Additionally, it can be recycled to gain crafting materials. Raiders can obtain Rope by scavenging in Residential and Commercial areas, or by purchasing it from Celeste.

items.name: Rosary
items.description: May be worth a few coins.
items.article: The Rosary is a collectible item that holds value. Raiders can sell it for coins or recycle it to obtain other resources. It shares its category with similar items such as a Rubber Duck, Silver Teaspoon Set, Statuette, Torn Book, or Vase.

items.name: Rotary Encoder
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Rotary Encoder is a rare item that Raiders can recycle into useful crafting materials. It is also required to complete the quest With a View. You can find Rotary Encoders by scavenging within the Stella Montis map.

items.name: Rubber Bands
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

items.name: Rubber Duck
items.description: Always there to lend an ear, should you need it.
items.article: The Rubber Duck is a common trinket that offers both a way to personalize your personal space and a practical use during your raids. You can collect these ducks and place them in your stash to decorate your Raider Den, making your base feel more like home. In the field, you can throw it to create a sound, effectively distracting nearby ARCs. This can be a useful tactic to draw attention away from your position or to lure them into a more favorable engagement area. You can find these trinkets inside chimneys when the Bird City event is active.

items.name: Rubber Pad
items.description: Can be recycled into rubber parts.
items.article: A Rubber Pad is a material intended for recycling into crafting materials. Its main purpose is to be processed at the Refiner. The resulting materials are used in crafting various components for mechanical and electrical projects.

items.name: Rubber Parts
items.description: Used to craft a wide range of items.
items.article: Rubber Parts are a basic crafting material essential for creating a wide array of useful items. You can find Rubber Parts by searching through mechanical, industrial, and electrical areas across the maps. They can also be obtained by recycling salvage. Furthermore, this material is sometimes available for purchase from Celeste, a vendor.

items.name: Ruined Accordion
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Ruined Accordion is a rare item Raiders can find while scavenging. Its main purpose is to be recycled, providing general crafting materials. These materials are helpful for creating various items and for different upgrades, which aids Raider progression. You typically obtain this item by exploring and searching containers or other points of interest in various areas of the map.

items.name: Ruined Augment
items.description: An augment ruined beyond repair.
items.article: The Ruined Augment is an augment that is too damaged to be equipped or used. Its primary purpose is to be recycled, providing useful crafting materials. This item is obtained exclusively by looting knocked-out Raiders. Augments degrade when their owner is knocked out, losing 30% durability with each instance. It becomes a Ruined Augment after its owner has been knocked out four times.

items.name: Ruined Baton
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Ruined Baton is an uncommon, damaged item. Similar to Ruined Handcuffs or Ruined Parachute, it serves as a component that can be recycled for various resources or sold for coins. Raiders also keep this item for use in crafting projects.

items.name: Ruined Emperor Beacon
items.description: This beacon no longer has any power to send a signal.

items.name: Ruined Handcuffs
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: Ruined Handcuffs are a damaged item. They can be sold for coins or recycled into other general resources. Similar items that serve this purpose include the Ruined Parachute and Ruined Riot Shield.

items.name: Ruined Parachute
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Ruined Parachute is a resource Raiders can use as a source for crafting materials. Its main purpose is to be recycled, which breaks it down into various resources. These resources are useful for creating other items and supplies that help Raiders as they explore and progress.

items.name: Ruined Riot Shield
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Ruined Riot Shield is a non-functional piece of equipment that Raiders can discover in the game world. Its primary purpose is to be recycled, which transforms it into useful crafting materials for other projects. Raiders can obtain this item by scavenging within various security areas they encounter while exploring.

items.name: Ruined Tactical Vest
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Ruined Tactical Vest is an uncommon item that Raiders can recycle to obtain crafting materials. When recycled, it yields 550 coins.

items.name: Rusted Bolts
items.description: Can be recycled into metal parts.
items.article: Rusted Bolts are an uncommon item. Their primary purpose is to be recycled, providing crafting materials. Raiders can obtain these bolts by searching specific locations while exploring the different maps. They are often associated with projects like the Trophy Cabinet Project Headwinds.

items.name: Rusted Gear
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article:
Rusted Gear is a rare resource in ARC Raiders used for Gunsmith upgrade. Rusted Gears spawn primarily inside vehicles with intact hoods and industrial containers across all maps.

Best Rusted Gear Farming Locations:

  • Dam Battlegrounds — The Controlled Access Zone currently has the highest Rusted Gear spawn rate in the game. Also check the buses and cars next to northern extract and service trucks in the Scrapyard.

  • Blue Gate — Checkpoint and Underground garage beneath the warehouse packed with searchable vehicles.

  • Spaceport — Focus on rocket assembly and vehicle maintenance areas.

  • Stella Montis — Green breachable containers in the Loading Bay.

Tips to Maximize Rusted Gear Drops: Prioritize zones tagged "Industrial" on the map. Breach vehicles with closed hoods. Run night raids for higher spawn rates and better loot quality.

items.name: Rusted Shut Medical Kit
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article:
The Rusted Shut Medical Kit is a damaged version of a Medical Kit. Its rusted and shut state indicates it is not functional as a regular healing item.

Raiders obtain this item from loot or as a quest reward.

items.name: Rusted Tools
items.description: Can be recycled into metal parts.
items.article: Rusted Tools are rare items primarily used to upgrade your Gunsmith, which helps improve your crafting capabilities. These tools can also be recycled into crafting resources. You can obtain them by scavenging from containers.

items.name: Rusty ARC Steel
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: Rusty ARC Steel is a material that Raiders collect to use in recycling. It is a worn-out version of ARC Performance Steel. To find Rusty ARC Steel, you need to defeat different types of ARCs or search through the remains of ARCs that have already been destroyed. When you recycle this item, you will obtain general crafting components and coins.

items.name: Sample Cleaner
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Sample Cleaner provides useful resources. Its main use is to be recycled into crafting materials. You can find Sample Cleaners by scavenging in the Stella Montis map.

items.name: Scout Patrol Note
items.description: A note seemingly documenting patrol schedules and access codes.

items.name: Secret Meeting Info
items.description: Thorough documentation of secret meetings held by researchers around the Stella Montis facility.

items.name: Seed Vault Box Key
items.description: A key opening a specific box in Stella Montis' Seed Vault.

items.name: Seeker Grenade
items.description: A homing grenade that targets a single nearby ARC dealing explosive damage on impact.
items.article:
The Seeker Grenade is a throwable item that automatically finds and targets a single nearby ARC, exploding upon impact to deal damage. It is useful for taking down smaller flying ARCs like Wasps, Hornets, Fireflies, and Snitches.

Raiders can obtain this grenade by crafting it at an Explosives Station using the Seeker Grenade Blueprint. It can also be purchased from the vendor Apollo. It functions as a smaller version of the Wolfpack.

items.name: Seeker Grenade Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Seeker Grenade
items.article: The Seeker Grenade Blueprint is a blueprint that unlocks the ability to craft seeker grenades at the Refiner, providing you with more options for dealing with ARCs during your raids.

items.name: Sensors
items.description: Used in crafting.
items.article: Sensors are a material primarily used in crafting at stations like the Explosives Station and Utility Station. They are also needed for certain projects. You can obtain Sensors by looting arcs such as the Snitch and Surveyor, and by looting Androids. They are also found by scavenging from Server Rack containers. Additionally, Sensors are available for purchase from Celeste using coins, or by recycling salvage.

items.name: Sentinel Firing Core
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Sentinel Firing Core is a Rare component salvaged from ARCs. Its primary use is as a crafting material for upgrading your Gunsmith station from level 2 to level 3. You can obtain this item by looting arcs like the Sentinel and the Courier. This item can also be recycled for crafting materials.

items.name: Sextant
items.description: Once thought to be a rudimentary spaceship prototype, it is claimed by the Nomads to be a sophisticated method for documenting one’s travels.

items.name: Shaker
items.description: A rhythmic instrument used to attract ARC's attention, and impress other Raiders.
items.article:
The Shaker is an Uncommon Gadget that plays one of two melodies. It is used to attract ARCs or to play music with other Raiders who have instruments like the Recorder or Acoustic Guitar. Using it prevents actions that require both hands.

You can obtain the Shaker in a few ways:

  • Craft it using crafting materials (requires the "Traveling Tinkerer" Inventory Skill).
  • Find it by scavenging in residential areas.
  • Purchase it from Shani for 40 coins (limit of three per day).
  • Get it from specific Raider Decks, such as the Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie.

You can repair the Shaker with crafting materials or recycle it for resources.

items.name: Sheet Metal
items.description: Used in crafting.

items.name: Shield Recharger
items.description: A handheld kit that gradually recharges shield over time.
items.article:
The Shield Recharger is a handheld kit used to gradually restore your shield over time. When activated, it recharges 4 shield points per second for 10 seconds, adding up to 40 shield points in total. This amount is enough to fully replenish a Light Shield.

Raiders can craft a Shield Recharger at Workbench, which requires a Medical Lab to be unlocked. Alternatively, it can be crafted directly in your inventory if you have the 'In-Round Crafting' skill. It can also be purchased from Lance for 1,560 coins.

items.name: Shield Stress Testing
items.description: Sustained damage could reveal exactly what makes a shield give out—and how to make that happen faster. For science, naturally.

items.name: Shotgun Ammo
items.description: Shotgun shells used for shotguns.
items.article:
Shotgun Ammo is a type of ammunition used exclusively by shotguns. It helps penetrate ARC armor more easily than light ammo, but it is not as effective as medium ammo.

Raiders can obtain Shotgun Ammo in several ways:

  • By scavenging or finding it in Raider Caches.
  • By looting arcs.
  • It can be crafted at the Workbench.
  • It is also sold by Tian Wen.

items.name: Shotgun Choke I
items.description: Slightly reduces base dispersion.

items.name: Shotgun Choke II
items.description: Moderately reduces base dispersion.
items.article:
Shotgun Choke II is a Weapon Mod that reduces how much shotgun pellets spread when fired. Attaching this mod makes your shotgun shots land in a tighter pattern, helping you hit targets more accurately.

You can obtain Shotgun Choke II by scavenging it in the environment, crafting it at a Gunsmith with the Shotgun Choke II Blueprint, or purchasing it from Tian Wen. It can be recycled to gain resources.

items.name: Shotgun Choke II Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Shotgun Choke II
items.article: The Shotgun Choke II Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Shotgun Choke II weapon modification at the Gunsmith. This modification helps improve shotguns by reducing how much their shots spread.

items.name: Shotgun Choke III
items.description: Significantly reduces base dispersion.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Il Toro, Vulcano

items.article: The Shotgun Choke III is an attachment for shotguns that helps make your shots spread less, increasing their accuracy. It also makes the weapon last longer before needing repairs. You can craft it at a Gunsmith bench once you have the Shotgun Choke III Blueprint.

items.name: Shotgun Choke III Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Shotgun Choke III
items.article: The Shotgun Choke III Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a weapon mod at the Gunsmith bench level 3. This mod helps shotguns fire pellets in a tighter pattern, making their shots more focused.

items.name: Shotgun Silencer
items.description: Moderately reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.
items.article:
The Shotgun Silencer is a weapon modification that moderately reduces the noise your shotgun makes when fired. It specifically reduces sound by 50%, making your shots quieter. This modification can be used with shotguns.

You can craft it at a Gunsmith bench using a Shotgun Silencer Blueprint. It can also be recycled or salvaged to recover other resources.

items.name: Shotgun Silencer Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Shotgun Silencer. Moderately reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.
items.article: The Shotgun Silencer Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Shotgun Silencer at the Gunsmith. This weapon modification is designed to reduce the amount of noise your shotgun makes when fired and is compatible with shotguns. The blueprint itself can be recycled for resources.

items.name: Showstopper
items.description: A grenade that detonates after a delay, stunning enemies within its radius.
items.article: The Showstopper is a type of grenade that stuns ARCs and other Raiders within its blast area. It detonates after a short delay or immediately upon hitting a target. You can find this item by scavenging, or by crafting it at an Explosives Station. Crafting requires you to first learn the Showstopper Blueprint.

items.name: Showstopper Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Showstopper.
items.article: The Showstopper Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Showstopper grenade at an Explosives Station. This grenade is designed to stun ARCs and other Raiders within its blast radius of 6 meters. It detonates after a 3.5-second delay, stunning ARCs for 7 seconds and Raiders for 2 seconds.

items.name: Shrapnel Grenade
items.description: A makeshift fuze grenade that bursts into razor-sharp fragments upon detonation.
items.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating.
items.article: The Shrapnel Grenade is a throwable item that explodes, scattering razor-sharp fragments. It deals damage to those caught in its blast, but it is less effective against the armor of ARCs. You can get this grenade by scavenging or by crafting it at an Explosives Station level 2. It can also be recycled to recover various materials.

items.name: Shredder Gyro
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

guide_links.label: Deal Damage to Shredders: Weekly Trial

items.article: A Shredder Gyro is a component scavenged from defeated Shredders, a type of ARC. This item plays a role in crafting and maintaining your gear. You can use it as a component when crafting at a Gunsmith. It is also needed to repair weapons, helping to keep them in good condition. Furthermore, Shredder Gyros are required for various projects and can be recycled into salvage.

items.name: Signal Amplifier
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
items.article: The Signal Amplifier is a useful resource item primarily used for its component parts. Its main role is to provide crafting materials when you recycle it, which are essential for making different items. You can find Signal Amplifiers by scavenging inside containers, which are commonly located across Stella Montis.

items.name: Silencer I
items.description: Slightly reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.
items.article: The Silencer I is a weapon modification that reduces the sound your weapon makes when fired. This item is crafted at the Gunsmith once you have the Silencer I Blueprint.

items.name: Silencer I Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Silencer I
items.article: The Silencer I Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Silencer I weapon mod at a Gunsmith Bench level 2. This mod helps reduce the amount of noise your weapon makes when you fire it. The blueprint itself can be recycled for coins and other resources.

items.name: Silencer II
items.description: Moderately reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest

items.article: The Silencer II is a weapon mod that makes your fired shots quieter. This helps you avoid attracting nearby ARCs when you use your weapon. To obtain this mod, you must first find its Silencer II Blueprint, which can be crafted at a Gunsmith bench. It can also be recycled or salvaged to recover general resources and components.

items.name: Silencer II Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Silencer II
items.article: The Silencer II Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a Silencer II weapon mod at a Gunsmith Bench. This mod helps reduce the sound your weapon makes when firing.

items.name: Silencer III
items.description: Significantly reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest

items.article: The Silencer III is a weapon modification that makes your shots much quieter. This modification reduces the noise your weapon makes by 60%, helping you remain hidden from ARCs during combat. While it offers quieter firing, it also causes your weapon to wear out 20% faster. It is compatible with many weapons, including the Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, and Tempest. You can recycle it to obtain other resources.

items.name: Silver Teaspoon Set
items.description: A shining, shimmering set of refinement and elegance.
items.article: The Silver Teaspoon Set is considered a valuable item, often described as showing refinement and elegance. It helps Raiders progress by being sold to Traders for coins, which are essential for various purchases and upgrades. Trinkets like this set are also frequently used to complete different projects.

items.name: Simple Gun Parts
items.description: Used to craft weapons.
items.article:
Simple Gun Parts are a common material for crafting, upgrading, and repairing many types of weapons. They can also be refined into more specialized components at a Refiner. These parts are used in crafting various items at a Gunsmith or Workbench.

You can find Simple Gun Parts by scavenging or by salvaging them from defeated ARCs including Wasps, Hornets, Turrets, Sentinels, and Shredders. They can also be bought from the vendor Celeste or obtained by recycling other materials.

items.name: "Sirena Dorata" Ship Model
items.description: With the Mediterranean sun glistening off its hull, this vibrant yacht is the timeless epitome of saltwater splendour.
items.article: The "Sirena Dorata" Ship Model is a decorative item found within the game. It serves as a collectible that Raiders can discover.

items.name: Skulker Driver
items.description: Drops from Meerkat.

items.name: Skulker Targeter
items.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

items.name: Smoke Grenade
items.description: A grenade that creates a lingering smoke cloud on impact, blocking visibility from ARC and other Raiders.
items.article:
A Smoke Grenade is a throwable item that releases a thick smoke cloud on impact. This cloud blocks the sight of ARCs and other Raiders, providing a way to escape or approach unseen. It lasts for 20 seconds and covers a 7.5-meter radius.

You can craft this item at a Workbench or Utility Station once you have learned the smoke grenade blueprint and gathered the necessary crafting materials. Apollo also sells the Smoke Grenade for 3,000 coins, with a daily limit of 6.

items.name: Smoke Grenade Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Smoke Grenade
items.article: A Smoke Grenade Blueprint allows you to craft smoke grenades at a Workbench or Utility Station, which create a cloud to block visibility from ARCs and other Raiders. It can be found by looting containers in Buried City as well as other maps during Night Raid or Cold Snap game types.

items.name: Smoke Grenade Trap
items.description: A laser trip wire that detonates a Smoke Grenade.
items.article:
A Smoke Grenade Trap is a device that projects a visible red laser up to five meters. When its laser beam is interrupted, it detonates a Smoke Grenade, releasing a thick gray smoke cloud. This smoke helps to hide Raider movements and obstructs the view of both ARCs and other Raiders.

You can place this device on almost any surface, but its laser is clearly visible to everyone. If a trap has not yet detonated, the Raider who placed it can disarm and pick it up.

This trap is crafted at the Workbench, requiring certain components and the "Traveling Tinkerer" skill.

items.name: Snap Blast Grenade
items.description: A grenade that sticks to surfaces, dealing explosive damage after a short delay.
items.article:
The Snap Blast Grenade is a magnetic grenade that sticks to surfaces before exploding after a short delay, dealing explosive damage. It is used in the Sparks Fly quest.

You can find this item in several ways:

  • By scavenging.
  • From containers such as Raider Caches, Security Lockers, and Weapon Cases.
  • By purchasing from Apollo for 2,400 coins, with a daily limit of 3.

This grenade can be crafted at an Explosives Station. It can also be recycled for resources.

items.name: Snap Hook
items.description: A gadget that allows the user to scale structures and cover large distances.
items.article: The Snap Hook is a gadget that helps you move quickly across areas by grappling to higher ground or managing descents. You can get a Snap Hook by completing the Lost In Transmission quest. It can also be crafted at a Utility Station once you have learned the Snap Hook Blueprint. Additionally, Snap Hooks are rewarded from certain Projects, such as Stage 5 of the Trophy Display. You can also find them listed in Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager and Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie.

items.name: Snap Hook Blueprint
items.description: Lets you craft a Snap Hook
items.article:
The Snap Hook Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to build the Snap Hook, which allows you to move quickly across distances or reach higher spots. Once learned, you can craft it at a Utility Station.

You can find this blueprint during Electromagnetic Storm map condition on various maps, most commonly in Residential loot areas.

items.name: Snitch Scanner
items.description: Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.

guide_links.label: Damage Flying-based ARC Enemies: Weekly Trial

items.article:
The Snitch Scanner is a utility item you can throw to call in Wasps. Once thrown, it becomes damaged.

You obtain this item by defeating Snitches, which are a type of ARC enemy.

It is used to upgrade your Utility Station and is also an item needed to complete The Trifecta quest. Additionally, you can recycle it for salvage.

items.name: Snowball
items.description: A compact snowball fashioned out of the most malleable and aerodynamic snow.

guide_links.label: Throw Snowballs at Bastions: Weekly Trial
Throw Snowballs at Rocketeers: Weekly Trial

items.article: A Snowball is a compact, throwable item fashioned from malleable and aerodynamic snow. It deals minor damage and can be used to complete various tasks or Weekly Trials, such as throwing them at Rocketeers. Raiders obtain Snowballs by collecting them from Snow Piles. These piles appear on maps when the Cold Snap map modifier is active.

items.name: Solid-Core Casting Tech
